x-research-tools.description: Offline development utility, separate from the whatsapp-cli control API; no HTTP route. Decodes complete protobuf-lite descriptors with variable-width scalar-presence and repeated entries, UTF-16 integer continuation/overflow checks, header/count validation and exact field-name pairing. Excludes bitFieldN_ bookkeeping names. Unsupported oneof mapping, malformed/truncated input, ambiguous descriptors or name mismatches are diagnosed on stderr without printing a partial pairing. Existing utility parameters remain positional APK and required --class. APK 2.26.37.71 BX5 mixes repeated strings and scalar int64 fields; fixed-triple decoding was refuted. BZc still decodes all 110 Message fields. Existing offline descriptor-inspection command; no HTTP route or runtime verification capability. APK 37.71 BWE fields: userJidString=1 (string), verified=2 (bool), verifiedIdentityKey=3 (bytes), actionSeq=4 (int64); BT5 verified=1 (bool), actionSeq=2 (int64). BZb ProtocolMessage markAsVerifiedAction=32 is nested under BZc Message protocolMessage=12. These are recovered schema facts, not a served endpoint or implemented receive policy. Inbound action application is companion-only, requires LID/non-self target, 32-byte key, all field presence and a strictly newer sequence >=1; local metadata writing rechecks identity under lock. Complete serialization, UI triggers and client verification implementation remain unfinished. Evidence: docs/protocol/peer-identity.md. Since 2026-10-13 names are paired by following the newMessageInfo objects array through static helper bodies read from the same APK (the retained-proto-fields simulator), not by literal order; a class that cannot be followed is refused naming the call, and --literal-order prints the old method-order pairing labelled unverified. Not yet run against an APK: tested on retained 2.26.37.71 bodies and synthetic DEX-method input only. Helper bodies are matched on the call's checked full descriptor; an APK scan failure is reported on stderr rather than as an absent method.

Offline development utility, separate from the whatsapp-cli control API; no HTTP route, no APK needed. Reads a committed research disassembly (docs/protocol/apk/**.txt) and follows the straight-line code that builds a protobuf-lite dynamicMethod's newMessageInfo objects array: registers, new-array, aput-object, and static helpers whose bodies are retained from the same APK, matched by the file's SHA-256 header and the call's full descriptor (a shorty-only call is not followed; disagreeing retained copies make the call count as not retained, so the class is refused). The packed-switch fans out; exactly one newMessageInfo call site and exactly one reaching case are required. Every slot must be written once with a field name or class/verifier object, the leading slots must be exactly the descriptor's presence-word count of bitFieldN_ names, and the name count must equal the decoded descriptor's; an array escaping into another array or a field, an instruction rendered without its destination register and an unknown opcode all refuse. Refusals go to stderr naming the reason, including the helper whose body is not retained. --helpers sets the directory searched for helper bodies (default: the bundle directory's parent, only when that is docs/protocol/apk; otherwise --helpers is required). Symlinks are not followed. --literal-order also prints, under a header marked LITERAL ORDER, unverified, the apk-proto-fields method-order pairing for a refused class. APK 2.26.37.71 retained files decode exactly for BZc Message (110), BZD ImageMessage (29), BZB DocumentMessage (21), BZE VideoMessage (30), BZ0 AudioMessage (16), BZK Conversation (59), BY9 PreKeySignalMessage (8), GsB ADVDeviceIdentity (5), 6tK, BSo and BP2 (BSp is literal-order only: its helper call is retained as a shorty); literal order is refuted for BZB, where helper Ayp.A1K writes fileSha256_ at objects[4]. BZc gives pinInChatMessage=63; the BVD PinInChatMessage descriptor is not retained, so pin sending is not implemented. Evidence: docs/protocol/apk-analysis.md#field-numbers-from-retained-bundles-retained-proto-fields-2026-10-13.

Offline DEX developer disassembler; no HTTP route. Direct DEX class_def_item superclass_idx is now printed as # extends for matching method classes, using checked type lookup and NO_INDEX=<none>; inherited method ownership is not guessed. APK 37.71 9Np directly extends BaseMexCallback, closing its C2c dispatch link. Versioned bundle bytes remain unchanged by this CLI-only header addition. Names APK identity metadata reads (iget-wide, iget-boolean, iget-byte) and safety-number arithmetic (rem-long/2addr, and-long/2addr, or-long/2addr, shl-long/2addr), preserving byte offsets and operands. Literal 37.71 CjU/B7E-style fixtures verify widths and registers. Unknown opcodes remain explicitly marked. Does not unpack native superpack containers or claim native algorithm recovery. APK 37.71 verification writes now name iput-boolean (0x5c) and iput-wide (0x5a), retaining existing 22c registers, field references and instruction widths. Literal Cg3.A00 instructions at classes7.dex 0x5fc138/0x5fc180 provide regression coverage. This is offline research tooling, not an implemented human-verification commit API. Static 37.71 contact exclusion reproduction also covers 1lL/0bo/0lr/C0F: hosted device-account and identity-attestation SQL sources use distinct enums, and contact-state value 2 remains semantically unknown. Native display getter evidence distinguishes full LID QR bytes from parsed LID-user display input; no runtime fingerprint or human-verification capability is added. APK 37.71 JhJ/CSC/0bN/KXj/26B/Cbb traces establish peer identity-map cardinality, hosted-99 class filtering, distinct local key controls and a contact-state predicate {1,2,3}; active runtime values remain unknown. Relative code-unit jump annotations now use explicit signed magnitudes for goto/goto16/goto32 and conditional branches, fixing misleading plus-prefixed two's-complement negatives. APK 37.71 JhJ.A0Z at 02d0/02d4 returns to 022c, separating PN-input selection from the later captured/contact V3/V4 gate. Literal/minimum/truncation regressions cover the formatter; static evidence in docs/protocol/fingerprint-input-selection-evidence.txt. Scheme, username and nullable PN-sharing producers are documented; current account values and native V3 comparison remain unverified. APK 37.71 FetchTruncatedGroupsJob.A0G memory arithmetic now names mul-double/2addr (cd) at 003c and div-double/2addr (ce) at 0042 using existing 12x register/width decoding. Literal instruction and truncated-prefix regression covers the correction. Static group refresh context, IQ/MEX request serializers and inherited dispatch ordering are recorded in docs/protocol/groups.md; runtime notification application, complete ACK serialization and current feature selection remain unimplemented or unknown. No new control command or HTTP route. Empty method-body results now report active class and optional method filters rather than claiming class absence; inherited APK 37.71 9R2 callbacks are the observed static counterexample. Group batch response union and current Cp2 ACK writer are documented offline; no runtime notification application or HTTP route is added. APK 37.71 base handler BFC to CmG.A02/A00 now establishes incoming notification from/id/participant/type metadata; recipient/category/edit belong to a separate receipt wrapper. Normal-edge 0yv.A09 analysis establishes initial dirty refresh round zero and zero group-pair integer, whose meaning remains unknown. Alternate executor and upstream group dispatch remain untraced. Evidence docs/protocol/group-notification-input-evidence.txt; no runtime group notification scheduling or route added. Binary-operation operand formatting now covers the existing-width 23x opcode range 0x90..0xaf, fixing missing registers on named add-int without extending mnemonic coverage. Literal APK 37.71 job bytes at classes6.dex 0x673e42 independently verify participant-sum operands/comparison and high-register/truncated fixtures cover the format. Job participant-estimate partitioning, returned-size replacement/fallback, null round-bound calculation and alternate Fpc notification executor are traced in docs/protocol/group-refresh-partition-evidence.txt. Automatic dirty refresh and its error/rate-limit response application remain unfinished; no live validation or HTTP route added. Typed 23x binary opcode names cover 0x90..0xaf (int/long/float/double arithmetic and shifts), following AOSP. Literal APK 37.71 group timestamp multiplication/division fixtures validate long operations; this reports bytecode rather than executing arithmetic or establishing wire time units. Signed 21s const/16 and const-wide/16 annotations now preserve raw hexadecimal bits and add negative decimal meaning: 37.71 0Xx.A02+00ba 16 02 ff ff is -1, not a positive row ID. Literal sentinel/minimum-value regression fixtures retain instruction boundaries. APK 37.71 8kY.A0B time arithmetic now names bd mul-long/2addr using existing 12x operands/widths. Independent classes6.dex 0x26374c literal bytes 1600e803bd021002 verify multiplier 1000, multiply v2 by v0 and return-wide. Full selected 0Xo.A03 source documents four __typename hash branches, required group/participants/properties and nullable subject, distinct time/version paths and feature-0x36fe creator LID/country metadata. Wire names, complete A4m mapping, Java catch/coercion and durable group conversion/application remain unfinished. This is offline annotated research, not a new runtime response schema or live capability. Evidence docs/protocol/mex-group-converter-evidence.txt and docs/protocol/mex.md. --exceptions renders checked code_item try_item/encoded_catch_handler_list metadata as ordered typed catches and final catch-all, explicit try-range count including zero, half-open ranges/targets explicitly in 16-bit code units. Metadata validation applies to all matching nonnative method bodies; default output and versioned bundle format unchanged. Rejects malformed padding, overlapping/unordered/out-of-range try ranges, handler offsets not pointing to parsed starts, bad type/target indices, truncation and signed/unsigned catch LEB overflow before any method output. The previous warning-and-partial-result DEX scanner now propagates file-qualified errors; two-DEX regression covers malformed bytes and invalid catch metadata after valid methods. No Throwable hierarchy, instruction-boundary or whole-DEX verification claimed. APK 37.71 0Gv.A01 NumberFormatException over code units 7..12 returns the supplied default at 12; LbE.A04 catches four reflection exceptions to null-return handler. Independent literal code_item regression is docs/protocol/mex-long-parser-catch-fixture.json. A4m constructor maps group type to A03, separate creation/subject/version/appeal long fields and map/boolean argument slots; full coercion and durable group application remain unfinished. These are offline source facts, no HTTP route or live response fields. Full core bundle audit refreshed a single noise-handshake op=bd annotation from unknown to mul-long/2addr, with identical opcode/offsets/operands and 21 other topics unchanged; only its source/checksum changed. This corrects presentation, not handshake behavior. Core 27 files/731494 bytes; comparison docs/protocol/apk/core-mul-long-rendering-diff.json against Git 34b5ab5. Static APK 37.71 outer prekey research now separates the STATELESS actor (B77.A04, fresh DS0 session map and no-op DRz.COt) from ordinary durable stores and companion identity admission. Messaging CoU.A04 reaches 11T.A0D before CQn.A00 dispatch to 0jc.A0O; the selected DOL gate is voice-call specific. Typed catches bind obfuscated exception classes to local result codes, not recognized server responses or retry authority. Existing --exceptions and apk-callers reproduce the trace; no HTTP route, account mutation or new runtime companion-bootstrap capability. Full sender/ADV/address producers and admission conditions remain unknown. Evidence: docs/protocol/peer-identity.md#outer-prekey-dispatch-and-companion-admission-2026-10-07. Static APK 37.71 new-device membership trace: 11T.A0D remote path removes already present addresses before add-only user_device inserts; different newer index does not overwrite a held address here. 1IW.A02/A09 gated canonical selection and AzR.A00 rebinding remain distinct from full signed-list time. B7j.A00/A03 read/write membership; teardown caller Boolean and participant/observer side effects remain incompletely traced. Existing commands reproduce preserved full methods. No new Rust admission, HTTP route, live request or account mutation. Evidence docs/protocol/peer-identity.md#companion-new-device-membership-application-2026-10-08. Opcode b2 now renders mul-int/2addr using existing width/register decoding; literal 37.71 0CK.A07 DEX window regression validates multiplication/branch boundaries. Static ordinary teardown producer is 0bq.A04 plus 1Uf dead_devices membership plus nonnull parsed message offline Integer, separate from retry count and dhash. Registry/reap lifecycle and new-device runtime remain unported. Existing smali/caller/field tools reproduce the full methods and selected callback contexts; no new live/HTTP capability. Evidence docs/protocol/peer-identity.md#companion-teardown-producer-and-registry-2026-10-08. Optional --signatures prints full declared method descriptors in comments and resolves ordinary invoke parameter/return descriptors, distinguishing overloads with identical shorties. Prototype/type-table bounds errors surface when requested; default shorty output is unchanged. Signed 11n const/4 now appends negative decimal meaning while preserving raw hex spelling: 0xff (-1) in APK 37.71 0Z8.A0G is the cache-clear sentinel, not 255. All sixteen literal nibbles have regression coverage. Existing versioned bundles preserve their original renderer bytes; new receipt-cache evidence uses the corrected renderer. No transport/runtime behavior or HTTP route changed. Evidence docs/protocol/receipt-cache.md. Negative DEX 22b/22s arithmetic literals now retain raw hexadecimal and add signed decimal, including 1gB.close -1 nesting adjustment; positive output and instruction widths are unchanged. Existing checksum generations remain immutable. Receipt-manager revoke exclusions and remaining unknowns: docs/protocol/receipt-manager.md. Opcode c2 now renders xor-long/2addr with the existing 12x width/register decoding, retaining unsigned comparison sign-bit transforms; this is a disassembler correction, not a messaging-runtime change. Packed and sparse switch annotations now retain every declared DEX u16-counted case rather than truncating after 64; malformed tails refuse explicitly. APK 37.71 1UE.A0R literal late bindings 2932/2946 and a sparse 65-case fixture cover visibility and tail validation. Old snapshots remain immutable; renderer changes can create annotation diffs on an unchanged APK, so compare releases exported by the same renderer. No runtime receipt or HTTP behavior changes. Evidence docs/protocol/receipt-ack-handlers.md. Fill-array payload preview now shows up to 256 data bytes and reports omitted byte counts for larger arrays. This preserves all 22 APK 37.71 receipt-status ranks; historical snapshots remain unchanged. No runtime admission or live capability is implied. Evidence docs/protocol/receipt-admission.md. DEX 21c static wide-field opcodes 0x61/0x68 now render sget-wide/sput-wide, with APK-derived byte and following-boundary regression tests. Operand/width behavior is unchanged. APK 37.71 scheduled-deadline evidence resolves D7g scheduled_time plus a 30-day millisecond constant; full downstream expiry policy remains unknown/unported. No new CLI flag, HTTP route, account or live behavior. Evidence docs/protocol/scheduled-deadline.md. Existing empty --class filter with --method BuN exposes all 80 exact BuN(LX/178;I)V declarations in APK 2.26.37.71; status-observer-declarations.json retains block hashes and scoped negative flags. This method-name inventory is not runtime observer registration or complete inheritance closure. Immediate post-hook is selector 16, not 5; see docs/protocol/status-observers.md. No account or network behavior changes.

Offline Qiling developer harness; no HTTP route or live account flow. Defaults to public ARM64 hello. decoder-init uses own-source asset/log/JNI adapters; unsupported asset/JNI operations abort. Requires JNI_OnLoad=0x10006, 19 registered methods and exit_group(0). decoder-first-entry invokes registered decompress_range_from_so with spo, /decoded and exclusive range [0,1); decoder-full-archive invokes ordinary decompress_from_so. Both extraction checks require an existing empty decoded directory and preserve partial outputs. The partial-range result is native 9/2, AssetDecompressionException and exit 7; full extraction under Qiling remains unverified after bounded timeouts and cancellation of a slower run when the separate QEMU runner succeeded. A parent subprocess enforces the wall limit (default 10 seconds); ARM64 basic blocks are conservatively charged across guest threads before execution (default 1000000 instructions). Qiling threaded run timeout/count alone were refuted as bounds. host-meminfo maps real host /proc/meminfo for local resource estimation. Empty guest environment; missing fixtures/dependencies and invalid bounds fail preflight. Proc-exe stat uses actual fixture metadata; munmap permits valid wholly unmapped ranges, rejects unaligned/zero-length input and delegates mapped ranges. trace-worker requires an extraction check and the exact 37.71 ARM64 decoder SHA-256; unknown layouts fail preflight. It reports at most 64 exceptional stage/offset, stream/type, declared/requested/produced counts and hash_check records. Pinned partial-range tracing shows stream 6 produced/declared=125448, requested=0, hash_check=0 and the oversized-file branch. Read-only futex observation reports up to 64 transitions as thread/local selector/op/val/timeout_present, collapsing consecutive duplicates without addresses. Instruction progress prints every 100 million charged. Maximum 600 seconds/10 billion instructions are local tooling budgets, not server limits. No native safety-number algorithm or Android application compatibility is established. Evidence and setup: docs/protocol/native-unpacking.md and tools/apk-research/README.md.

Sixteen offline developer checks: Qiling missing-fixture refusal, actual ARM64 hello exit, actual instruction exhaustion, parent wall-limit termination of an infinite ARM64 guest, preserving partial outputs in both extraction modes, rejecting unknown trace layouts. Rootfs-dependent Qiling cases skip when WARUSTAPI_LOADER_ROOTFS is absent; the infinite fixture requires Clang/LLD and compiles in a temporary directory. These tests do not execute the APK decoder or contact an account. Actual QEMU decoder initialization and full reconstruction were validated separately. Fingerprint checks cover missing library, rejecting a wrong hash before execution and optional actual pinned ARM64 synthetic control-flow execution. The last case skips without WARUSTAPI_FINGERPRINT_LIBRARY; SHA/MCF calls are modeled, not native primitives. No live account verification is performed. No whole QR comparison/native callback is executed by this suite. Two additional byte-check tests cover wrong-build preflight and actual pinned leaf execution with 862 synthetic comparisons; the latter skips without WARUSTAPI_FINGERPRINT_LIBRARY. No modeled callees in byte mode. Three V4 comparison checks additionally cover wrong/missing-build empty-output refusal and actual pinned core/helper/remapper execution versus the committed 115-case artifact. The actual case skips without WARUSTAPI_FINGERPRINT_LIBRARY. It uses modeled dependencies, not complete QR parsing/orientation or Android string behavior. Three additional string-mode checks cover paired-option and wrong string-fixture refusal plus actual pinned merged/Bionic comparison. That last case requires all three library variables and compares the 115 core codes to the original modeled artifact, plus compact actual-string counts and 268 ASCII/prefix cases. This suite has 22 cases with all four fixture variables set; none establish live human verification. Three native-parser tests add missing/wrong-build empty-output refusal and actual pinned 50-case unpack/free corpus reproduction. Actual case skips without WARUSTAPI_SCHEMA_LIBRARY. The fully configured suite now has 25 cases; modeled memory primitives remain explicit. The QEMU and schema preflight cases moved to xtask unit tests (cargo test -p xtask) with the Rust ports; 31 Python cases remain for the Unicorn/Qiling checkers.

Offline QEMU ARM64 developer runner, no HTTP route or account flow. Default decoder-init; decoder-full-archive invokes the unmodified APK 2.26.37.71 ordinary Superpack decompress_from_so entry with spo and /decoded. Pins decoder SHA-256 and, for full extraction, outer-container SHA-256. Requires local Bionic fixtures and the Rust decoder probe/import shims built from tools/apk-research/native-probe (no C), bwrap and qemu-aarch64-static. Refuses a nonempty or non-directory decoded destination before preparation, preserving existing files. Adds owner execute permission only to local probe/linker copies and prepares mount points. Bubblewrap uses network/PID namespaces, an empty environment, a read-only fixture root and only /decoded writable for extraction. The xtask parent enforces the wall limit and kills the sandbox (default 30 seconds, range 1..600); die-with-parent terminates the worker. No instruction budget is implemented for QEMU. Full extraction returned 80 names including duplicate libsodium.so, leaving 79 unique valid ARM64 shared ELF files totaling 62743576 bytes; a second extraction reproduced all 79 hashes. This runner does not execute the reconstructed WhatsApp libraries. Native fingerprint anchors and containing unwind ranges are located; a separate checker now validates shared hash control flow. Complete modern safety-number inputs, QR semantics and Java/wamsys dispatch remain unfinished. See docs/protocol/native-unpacking.md for hashes, exact build provenance, failures and unknowns. Rust port of the former native_qemu_check.py, verified 2026-11-01: decoder-init output identical to the Python runner, and the Rust-built probe reproduced all 79 extracted library hashes.

Offline pinned APK 2.26.37.71 ARM64 fingerprint hash control-flow check; no HTTP route or account flow. Requires exact reconstructed libwhatsapp.so SHA-256, Unicorn and pyelftools. Uses only built-in synthetic bytes; does not accept account identifiers or keys. Maps the shared V3/V4 hash routine page and intercepts six explicitly supported SHA/MCF entry points with host models. Unknown branches refuse. Two cases compare native ARM64 input ordering and loop count against 5200 SHA-512 rounds of previous-state plus constant second argument, counting 5200 finishes and 10400 updates. Per case bounds: one million instructions and ten seconds, with actual return PC required for success. Does not execute the full library, JNI/runtime, native cryptography, create/display/QR routines or establish a current account safety number or human verification. Exact addresses, modeled boundaries and unresolved producers are documented in docs/protocol/safety-number.md. Complementary static research now connects Java V4 creation/result selectors, PN/LID callbacks and 32-byte sorting versus 33-byte serialized key data. The traced Java result selector 4 passes QR serialization version 0; selector 5 passes 1. These paths are documented, not executed by this checker; UI scheme selection, inventory, individual QR fields/comparison and human verification remain unfinished. --check defaults to hash. bytes instead executes the actual 37.71 leaf byte comparator 0xc9bbfc..0xc9bd20 without modeled callees: 862 synthetic equal/mismatch cases cover zero length, vector/tail boundaries, serialized-key/digest lengths, every mismatch position through 66 bytes, selected positions at 4096 bytes, and shifted pointers. Inputs end at an unmapped page (one sentinel byte for shifted cases); unexpected branches or budget exhaustion fail. Each case must return within ten seconds/one million instructions. XOR/OR results and equal-length instruction counts are checked. No user input bytes or account data are accepted; this does not prove end-to-end constant time or full QR verification.

Offline APK 2.26.37.71 native fingerprint protobuf-C schema extractor; no HTTP route or live flow. Requires exact reconstructed merged-library SHA-256; a std-only ELF64 reader, no Python or pyelftools; executes no native instructions. Reads relocation-backed descriptors with ELF64 little-endian ARM64, file-backed extent, magic, count, optional-type, sorted-tag and native-offset checks. Missing/wrong builds refuse with no partial schema. Output metadata includes apk_build, library_sha256, evidence, messages (name/address/size/fields), and enums. Each field has name/tag/label/type/address/quantifier_offset/offset, plus nested message or enum names where applicable. FingerprintData tags: public_key=1 bytes, pn_identifier=2 bytes, lid_identifier=3 bytes, username_identifier=4 bytes, hosted_state=5 enum, hashed_public_key=6 bytes. CombinedFingerprint: version=1 uint32, local_fingerprint=2 message, remote_fingerprint=3 message. HostedState enum E2EE=0, HOSTED=1. Descriptor-optional status is distinct from runtime comparison requirements. Version zero uses serialized key inventory and version one its identifier-free digest. Does not parse user QR data, establish full comparison compatibility or change account verification. Reproducible output: docs/protocol/fingerprint-native-schema.json; serializer/comparison evidence: docs/protocol/safety-number.md. Rust port of native_schema_check.py; its output equals the committed JSON byte for byte, also as an xtask unit test when WARUSTAPI_SCHEMA_LIBRARY is set.

Offline static KEM trace for APK 2.26.37.71; no HTTP route, account or native execution. Pins libwhatsapp.so and libwhatsappmerged.so SHA-256, disassembles six fixed address ranges with the external llvm-objdump, checks JNI dispatch/size/32-byte randomness instruction anchors and writes or byte-compares seven retained files including manifest.json. Rust port of native_kem_trace.py; --check verified all seven committed files 2026-11-01. Evidence docs/protocol/native-kem.md.

Regenerates the independent synthetic hybrid initial-KDF (16) or Signal v3/v4 wire (24 signal, 8 prekey) vectors in docs/protocol from hmac/sha2 primitives and hand-encoded protobuf, never through whatsapp-api's HKDF or wire code. --check compares byte for byte; an xtask unit test does the same in CI. Synthetic inputs only: not APK execution, DH/KEM verification or encryption. Rust port of hybrid_kdf_vectors.py and signal_wire_vectors.py; output identical to the committed files.

Builds the deterministic case inputs and pipes them to the independent desktop Java protobuf oracles (docs/protocol/AdvDetailsProtoOracle.java, ProtocolEnumsOracle.java) under the pinned protobuf-javalite 4.36.1 JAR (SHA-256 verified); expected values come from Java, not the Rust parsers. adv-details reproduces CPython random.Random(3771) exactly for its 250 random cases. Requires java/javac locally; not run in CI. Rust port of the two docs/protocol generate_*_oracle.py scripts; 2026-11-01 output equalled crates/whatsapp-api/fixtures/prekeys/2.26.37.71-adv-details-oracle.json (637 cases) and -control-enum-oracle.json (2040 cases) byte for byte.

Existing offline DEX development utility; no HTTP route or account input. Reports exact class/method invoke sites with caller class, method shorty and DEX byte offset. Locates invocations, not interface implementations. APK 37.71 JniBridge.jvidispatchIOO has eleven sites; KXj.A01 has three callers. Sharing a dispatch name is not proof of sharing a selector or fingerprint semantics. Reproduce Java comparison selection and result-presentation traces in docs/protocol/safety-number.md.

Offline development utility, no HTTP route or account flow. Exact APK 2.26.37.71 reconstructed libwhatsapp.so SHA-256 required. Executes native V4 core, PN/username helpers and remapper on 115 built-in synthetic cases with modeled getters, key/LID equality and MCF/string primitives; accepts no account/scanned data. Actual branch codes, remapped codes, instruction counts and modeled string-call counts or intercepted invariant aborts are emitted as deterministic JSON matching docs/protocol/fingerprint-native-comparison-cases.json. All 81 hosted-state combinations, username presence/difference, PN omissions/mismatch, version-selected keys and remote LID mismatch are covered. Both scanned hosted states absent selects legacy success regardless of known states. Ten seconds/one million instructions per core/remap call; actual return PC required. Unexpected branches, wrong/missing builds and budget exhaustion refuse without partial output. Does not execute native protobuf parsing, conversion/orientation wrapper, JNI, Android libc, human verification or companion sync. Host ASCII lowercasing is only a synthetic string model. Static preceding converter rejects unknown hosted enums (-38); direct-core abort cases are invariant tests, not real QR crash claims. See docs/protocol/safety-number.md. Optional paired --string-library/--libc require exact pinned 37.71 merged and public Bionic hashes, replacing host string comparison with actual MCFStringCompare and Bionic strncasecmp instructions over synthetic object representation/TLS. Original 115 statuses agree (195 actual string comparisons; maximum 493 instructions), plus 268 actual native ASCII cases cover values 1..127, every mismatch position on both sides, prefix and empty variants and 256-byte inputs (maximum 2986 instructions). Output adds string_library_sha256, bionic_fixture_sha256, native_string_comparisons per core case and native_ascii_checks summary; compact observations in docs/protocol/fingerprint-native-string-check.json. Fixture is public comparison libc, not bundled APK or proof of all Android versions. Object construction and non-string dependencies remain modeled. Neither QR parser/orientation nor account state is exercised.

Offline developer utility, no HTTP route or account flow. Exact APK 2.26.37.71 merged-library SHA-256 required. Executes actual protobuf-C combined unpack, generated initializers, parsing/merge helpers and free over 50 built-in synthetic buffers; emits accepted flags, recognized presence/hex bytes/enum/version, native unknown-field counts, instruction counts and modeled allocation totals. No arbitrary/user/account payloads accepted. ELF PT_LOAD images and relevant internal relocations are mapped, but hook permits only identified parser/generated-init ranges and modeled allocator/free/memcpy/memset stubs. Empty input is accepted by this standalone parser; actual comparison wrapper separately aborts, while our client refuses empty as local policy. Ten seconds/one million instructions per unpack/free invocation, 64-KiB input and 1-MiB monotonically allocated guest heap bounds. Return PC and no live modeled allocations after free/rejection required. Unexpected branches/wrong builds/budget exhaustion refuse before partial JSON. Independent corpus docs/protocol/fingerprint-native-parser-cases.json disproves eight prost acceptance assumptions and validates the bounded schema decoder. This is not full JNI/QR comparison, device inventory or human verification. Evidence: docs/protocol/safety-number.md.

Offline DEX development utility, no HTTP route or account operation. Scans standard instance/static field read/write opcodes (iget/iput/sget/sput variants) against an exact declaring class, name and type. --writes-only excludes reads. Sorts DEX filenames for reproducible output. Outputs DEX file, referencing class/method/shorty, read/write opcode and absolute DEX byte offset; reports count on stderr, including zero results. Uses the shared method visitor with independently reset direct/virtual method deltas and skips instruction payloads. Malformed traversed field tables/instruction streams or missing classes*.dex refuse before stdout; this is not a general DEX verifier. Quickened odex offsets, native/reflection accesses and dynamic provenance are outside scope. APK 2.26.37.71 LX/0Da;->A04:I has 17 direct write sites; scoped contact-state evidence in docs/protocol/safety-number.md establishes external_user_state, not Signal attestation or QR HostedState. No active scheme or account metadata is changed. APK 2.26.37.71 incoming root-count evidence traces optional-zero versus present malformed signed-int parsing, CaF/Cih/Bp2 transfer and the one physical Cih.A02 writer. Rank/Android coercion and backoff duration remain unported; these are source facts, not new server-response output fields. --group-numbers requires --group-info and explicitly reveals private group_numeric_metadata: creation_scaled, subject_creation_scaled, announcement_version, all signed decimal strings preserving i64 precision. Default output remains redacted. Actual library projection requires InvokeGroupCallback and object xwa2_group_query_by_id; no full group validity or state application. Numeric projection follows ADv.A04/A05 -> 8kY.A0B -> 0Gv.A01 default-zero and wrapping times-1000, while ADv.A03/A4m.A08 version stays unscaled. Nullable/nonobject subject gives zero. Signed-decimal strings support ASCII signs and reference BMP digits via UTF-16, reject whitespace/prefix/fraction/exponent/overflow to zero; signed integral JSON is exact, floating/wider-unsigned/bool/null/array/object numeric results zero via inferred optString/parseLong semantics. Independent executed host Java 21.0.12.1+1 oracle covers 479 cases and all 65536 UTF-16 units, 370 digits/37 BMP blocks; not APK/Android execution. Actual Android SDK/Unicode and full JSON lexical parity remain unverified. Library numeric Debug hides values; failures include no raw private content and no partial stdout. No HTTP route, account access, MEX dispatch or snapshot mutation. Evidence docs/protocol/mex.md#numeric-group-projection-into-rust-2026-10-07. --edge-roles requires --group-info and adds group_participant_edge_roles, an ordered list of recognized enum values unrecognized/admin/member/superadmin for JSONObject edges. Missing/null/nonarray edges yields empty; nonobject entries skip; duplicates preserve order. Callback must permit A04 and both query group and participants must be objects; refusal diagnostics contain no private payload and produce no partial stdout even with --group-numbers. LbE.A0A/A09 uses optJSONArray then optJSONObject; 8yl constructor wraps the object. Role is read from edge, not nested participant; all nonstring role values become unrecognized. This field-only projection precedes ADv.A0D phash short-circuit and participant model/typename/JID validation, so it is not member count/map or authorization/state application. Default response inspection stays redacted and does not expose this list. Eighteen synthetic APK-branch fixtures cover both payload children, not live captures. Static class_def evidence confirms BotJid 0hh -> abstract 0ZX -> UserJid; no-method-body lookup did not mean absence. Complete member/JID/alias/feature application remains unfinished; scalar conversion is described below. Evidence docs/protocol/mex.md#participant-model-fields-and-object-edge-projection-2026-10-07. --participant-scalars requires --group-info and explicitly prints private group_participant_scalars: phash_match boolean and edges in object-edge order, each with join_time (positive signed decimal string or null) and group_history_sent (nullable boolean). APK 37.71 LbE.A0G/Ayj.A1R optInt==1 default then optBoolean; ADv.A0D join_time positive optInt -> 1xf.A17 long and present history -> 8kW.A0q. Missing/null history stays null; other unconvertible values become false. Signed integral JSON Numbers narrow low32 bits; floating Numbers and numeric strings parse/truncate/saturate through Double semantics, with invalid/NaN zero. Java string whitespace <=U+0020, decimal/exponent/type suffix, case-sensitive NaN/Infinity and hexadecimal p-exponent supported; hex rounding uses guard/sticky ties-to-even including subnormals. Independent executed pinned AOSP org.json commit de876a01b29230b877c9f408348c38a90ee724a5 with host Temurin21.0.12.1+1 oracle covers 408 cases; complete Android SDK/JSON lexical parity remains unverified. serde_json float_roundtrip fixes observed local 0.99999999999999994 ->1 misrounding; Java correctly remains below1. Debug hides scalar values. Shared callback/group/participants refusals use mex.group.participants, contain no payload and no partial stdout. Default inspection unchanged. This scalar projection still inspects edges when phash_match=true; it does not treat ADv.A0D null as empty, construct/apply a member map, reclassify identities or contact the server. Source/reference/regression docs/protocol/mex.md#participant-scalar-coercion-and-float-rounding-2026-10-07. --participant-members requires --group-info and explicitly reveals private group_participant_map: kind phash_match with members=null, or kind members with an ordered array. Each member has primary/lid/pn address objects (user, canonical server, kind); nullable aliases; role empty/admin/superadmin; positive join_time as a decimal string or null; nullable group_history_sent; nullable display_name. ADv.A0D phash short-circuits without reading edges; missing/null/nonarray edges become an empty map, nonobject edges and missing/nonobject participant models skip. Unknown model hashes skip. The two known Java UTF-16 hashes (bot c745b457, user 2179873b) are dispatched without invented server typename spellings; fixture names are synthetic hash probes. Invalid nullable bot JIDs skip and that branch ignores aliases/display_name. Strict user primary and present LID/PN aliases abort; later duplicate canonical primary keys replace values at first insertion position. Partial maps never reach stdout. LbE.A0E nullable optString now supports every shape accepted by the bounded strict JSON parser, using executed pinned-AOSP/host-Java references. Floating scalar text uses Java21 decimal selection and formatting; nested JSON numbers preserve distinct container negative-zero/integral-reduction rules. Structured values preserve original key order and replace duplicate values at the first key position, with JSONStringer slash/control escaping and literal printable Unicode. Scoped integer -0 classification yields 0; float -0.0 and quoted -0 remain distinct. Public data()/errors() retain the existing serde representation; the separate ordered source is private and Debug remains redacted. Decimal-selection or source invariants diagnose mex.participant.string_coercion without values; no supported form is deliberately refused as unimplemented. Runtime is not Java-dependent, no new package/version or global serde map-order feature was introduced. Bot, LID, PN, interop and traced user singletons retain strict type semantics; aliased identities do not merge distinct primary keys. Debug hides identifiers/content. Filtered interop alias and extra string constructor slots remain null in these branches and are not fabricated. This converter does not validate all group feature gates or apply a durable snapshot, settle an action or contact WhatsApp; downstream phash-null handling, complete Android runtime-version/lexical/cache parity and actual typename spellings remain unverified. Local member refusals name the offending id/lid/pn/display_name/__typename attribute without its private value.

Offline APK 2.26.37.71 MEX participant role conversion; no HTTP route, account access, live request or participant/state application. Optional --value supplies a nullable server string; omission, empty, unknown and whitespace-padded values resolve to unrecognized. LbE.A0C -> 4R7.A00 uses Locale.US uppercase without trimming and Enum.valueOf, with IllegalArgumentException fallback to 2hu.A05. ADMIN_MEMBER maps to admin, MEMBER to member, SUPERADMIN_MEMBER to superadmin; explicit UNSET_OR_UNRECOGNIZED_ENUM_VALUE maps to unrecognized. Unicode uppercase matches the 91 committed host Java reference cases (including dotless i and long s); complete Android SDK/Unicode version parity remains unverified. Output offline_only=true, role (unrecognized/admin/member/superadmin) and member_role (empty/admin/superadmin) only, never echoes the supplied value. Member and unrecognized remain distinct despite identical empty stored role. This string-only helper does not implement JSONObject optString coercions, participant hash guard, edge/JID conversion, full group validation or durable application. Evidence docs/protocol/mex.md#participant-role-conversion-and-member-map-boundaries-2026-10-07.

Offline APK 37.71 strict member-primary UserJid validation; no HTTP route, account access, sending eligibility or group-state application. Required --value is private input; success prints only offline_only=true and kind (phone, lid, bot, interop, server_zero, server_name, lid_me, status_me), never the supplied or canonical address. Failure has empty stdout and a content-free mex.participant.address diagnostic. Device suffixes, non-user domains and gdpr refuse. Phone/LID/bot constructor ASCII/length/prefix guards and interop last-hyphen/signed Integer.parseInt rules are preserved. Plain hosted/hosted.lid canonical domains normalize through explicit library server(); user() reveals private identifiers, while Debug hides them. Server/0 singletons and bare lid_me/status_me are accepted; bare server and @lid_me/@status_me domains refuse. Integer digit semantics validated against independent host Java, not Android Unicode-version parity. Full member assembly, alias application, Java cache effects and live MEX application remain unfinished. Evidence docs/protocol/mex.md.

Offline APK 37.71 member-storage scalar selection; no HTTP route, account access, clock read, membership reconciliation or durable write. Required --input is a private typed JSON object, local 16 KiB limit: required clock_ms signed i64; optional/null join_time and previous_join_time_ms signed i64, group_history_sent boolean, previous_history_state signed i32. Unknown/duplicate fields or invalid types refuse with content-free stderr and no partial stdout; missing/mistyped known fields are named without values, and unknown private keys are never echoed. Inputs are already converted 31c join/history metadata, not raw JSONObject coercion; normal ADv join producer is positive optInt widened to Long. Output offline_only=true, join_time_ms as exact signed decimal string, history_state nullable signed i32. Positive join_time multiplies by 1000 with Java wrapping; selection precedes multiplication so overflow never triggers fallback. Missing/nonpositive join preserves a positive previous millisecond timestamp, otherwise uses supplied clock_ms exactly. true history raises null or <2 to2; false raises null or0 to1 and preserves every other prior state including negative/higher values; null history preserves prior unchanged. Pure output Debug omits values. GroupParticipant::storage_metadata delegates its converted join/history fields to the shared helper. APK 0yw.A0X forwards A4m.A0O to A0U, whose null branch skips A00 membership reconciliation while other group-field updates continue; a nonnull empty map still enters reconciliation. This trace does not establish full alias/device/recovery/atomic group application. Independent executed host Java transcribed-branch corpus covers432 combinations, not APK/Android execution. Clock calibration and higher history-state meanings remain untraced. Evidence docs/protocol/mex.md#downstream-member-storage-and-null-map-2026-10-07.

Offline explicit private hash inspection, no HTTP route/account access/live feature selection or snapshot mutation. --input is a UTF-8 JSON array of strings, local limit 64 KiB/1024 entries; malformed/type/entry/address errors are content-free and produce no partial stdout. --version is required 1,2,3. V1 hashes supplied raw strings using SHA-1; V2/V3 parse the existing Rust Jid model and hash interpreted user/device/server components with SHA-256. V2 always renders user.0:device@server (literal agent zero); V3 renders user:device@server. Java UTF-16 sorting, concatenation without separators, first six digest bytes, standard Base64 and version prefix. Default collection mode preserves repeated entries, including distinct agents that render identically. --as-set explicitly prepares unique raw strings for V1 or unique Rust model addresses for V2/V3; this models producer preparation, not APK DeviceJid subtype/equality or complete membership validation. Output offline_only=true, version string, as_set boolean, input_count/hashed_count and explicit hash; never raw identifiers. Pure hashes are available without messaging crypto features in transport::participant_hash and re-exported from transport::groups for compatibility. Existing participant_hash_v2 convenience helper prepares a Rust address set then invokes the corrected V2 collection helper. New enum V2/V3 does not assert current feature 0x415b; automatic group sends retain V2. Explicit sender_key_stanza phash now accepts prefixes 1/2/3 with colon/maximum 32 bound; no new automatic sending or full Base64 validation is claimed. The planner now includes saved recipient devices and its known own primary; full own-companion inventory/account synchronization remains unfinished. group fanout-inspect exposes saved input counts and unknowns offline; active feature negotiation remains unfinished. UTF-8 encoding assumption/host Java 114-case/684-vector reference is not Android execution or strict APK JID validation. Source APK 37.71 1jL.A02/A05/A0N/A0O, AzR.A03, Ayj.A18/A19, DeviceJid.getRawStringWithNoAgent. Evidence docs/protocol/groups.md#participant-cache-and-versioned-hashes-2026-10-07.

Offline APK 2.26.37.71 JID-map row ranking using the actual Rust library selector; no HTTP route, account access, mapping write, alias authentication or cleanup dispatch. Required --input is typed private JSON: jid_row_id signed i64 and rows array; each row has signed i64 jid_row_id, lid_row_id and sort_id. Local limits 64 KiB/1024 rows; unknown fields, duplicate fields, missing fields and invalid types refuse with no partial stdout. Missing/duplicate known field names are reported; unknown private keys and values are never echoed. Output input_rows, matched_rows, distinct_sort_ids counts; selected boolean; nullable selected_lid_row_nonnegative and selected_lid_row_positive booleans; runtime_mapping_applied=false. Row IDs/sort values/JIDs are not printed; JidMapRow Debug is redacted. APK 0Xx.A01/A00 orders sort_id DESC,lid_row_id DESC, then 0eU reverse TreeMap overwrites equal sorts and picks its first value: greatest signed sort and smallest LID row ID at that sort. Preserve invalid winning values before downstream checks; no fallback to a lower-ranked valid candidate. Single 0Xw.A0C checks nonnegative selected LID, bulk A08 requires positive materialized row IDs; these booleans are diagnostics, not a successful mapping claim. sort_id timestamp meaning, row-authority/freshness, effective feature values and full runtime materialization remain unported. Independent executed SQLite cursor/reverse-map fixtures cover36 synthetic cases including all 24 permutations of a tie/cross-phone set, signed extremes, duplicates and invalid winners. Evidence docs/protocol/peer-identity.md and docs/protocol/jid-map-row-selection-fixtures.json.

Independent development fixture generator for the APK 2.26.37.71 JID-map row selector. Executes literal 0Xx.A01/A00 SQL over 36 synthetic SQLite cases, applies 0eU equal-sort replacement and greatest-sort selection, and writes docs/protocol/jid-map-row-selection-fixtures.json. --check compares exact fixture bytes without modifying them and refuses a mismatch. Uses Python standard-library SQLite only; no APK, account, network, private row input or Rust implementation is opened. This corpus verifies a transcribed SQL/collection algorithm, not Android execution, authenticated mapping authority or runtime PN/LID application.

Offline whole-APK file-content index; no HTTP route. Emits format-1 JSON with whole APK SHA-256/bytes and sorted paths to uncompressed file SHA-256/bytes. Reads every file through ZIP CRC verification without extracting or executing contents. Refuses duplicate/unsafe paths, corruption and tooling bounds. Does not verify APK signatures, recover methods or change account/profile state. Committed 2.26.37.71 baseline covers 14967 files. See docs/protocol/apk-file-diff.md.

Offline cached whole-APK index comparison; no HTTP route. Reports sorted added/removed/changed paths with old/new bytes and SHA-256, plus unchanged count and apk_container_changed. Validates format/hash/path/size and duplicate JSON file keys. No APK rescan, extraction, execution or automatic Rust patch. Cached self-comparison measured 0.211419 seconds locally; first indexing cost was 8.107389 seconds. This compares unmodified exported evidence, does not authenticate edited indexes or establish code semantics/signature validity/compatibility. See docs/protocol/apk-file-diff.md.

Offline development utility, separate from the whatsapp-cli control API; no HTTP route and no APK needed. Reads only the committed docs/protocol/apk/*/manifest.json and targets.json and writes docs/protocol/apk-coverage.json: retained bundles and topic counts per release (including the pinned 2.26.36.75, currently zero bundles), topics with evidence from more than one release, and whatsapp-api source files (generated proto excluded) cited or not cited by any retained topic, plus citations of files that no longer exist. --check fails if the committed report is stale. A release recorded with two APK hashes is refused. It measures retained bundle citations only: docs/protocol/rea envelopes, comments and protocol-document evidence are not counted, and unexported APK code is outside it. Evidence docs/protocol/apk-coverage.md.

info.title: WaRustAPI control API
info.description: This document describes every operation of the whatsapp-api library and whatsapp-cli. The x-transport field indicates whether an operation is served by whatsapp-cli serve over HTTP today or invoked through the CLI. The x-cli field gives the exact command. The x-library field names the Rust entry points behind each operation (crate path form); the whatsapp-cli test `openapi_library_symbols_exist` verifies they exist. The x-live field marks operations that contact WhatsApp servers and require explicit authorization via --allow-live-request. The HTTP control plane has no authentication and binds to loopback only.

Profile.name: profile
Profile.description: Named account profile (profiles-dir/NAME.json) supplying the store, account, key variable and config defaults; explicit flags win

Store.name: store
Store.description: Path of the account protocol database; defaults to protocol.redb

Account.name: account
Account.description: Local account identifier; defaults to default

KeyEnv.name: key-env
KeyEnv.description: Name of the environment variable holding the hex master key; defaults to WHATSAPP_API_MASTER_KEY

ProfilesDir.name: profiles-dir
ProfilesDir.description: Directory holding account profiles; defaults to lab/profiles

Config.name: config
Config.description: Private request configuration path; defaults to the profile's

LocalId.name: local_id
LocalId.description: Local message id (32 hex chars) from the send ticket

Conflict.description: Resource already exists, is reserved, or operation cannot proceed due to state conflict

Blocked.description: Operation blocked by server refusal, cooldown or preserved state

HistoryNoticeMetadata.description: History-notice metadata model returned by the pure decoder and carried on the received GroupHistoryNotice event. It is not a standalone HTTP response. Returns null for another message type, a metadata model for a supported notice, or a fixed redacted local error. No receiver addresses or opaque context/bot contents are retained. Positive count/window timestamp mirror APK 2.26.37.71 DA8.CF4. Timestamp units remain unknown. This helper does not authenticate or dispatch a notice.

message_count.description: Positive signed int64 count from BX5 field 3.

oldest_window_timestamp.description: Positive raw signed int64 window timestamp, BX5 field 2; unit unknown.

oldest_bundle_timestamp.description: Optional raw signed int64 bundle timestamp, BX5 field 5; unit and validity policy untraced.

receiver_count.description: Number of supported primary PN/LID history receivers; positive and locally limited to 1024.

non_receiver_count.description: Number of supported primary PN/LID non-history receivers; locally limited to 1024.

context_present.description: Opaque BV6 field 1 is present; its contents are not returned or validated.

bot_metadata_present.description: Opaque BV6 field 3 is present; its contents are not returned or validated.

PhoneNumber.description: Structured phone number with country code and national components

Jid.description: WhatsApp JID (Jabber ID) in form username@s.whatsapp.net for direct chats or username@g.us for groups

RequestId.description: Caller-supplied idempotency key; repeating the same request_id returns the saved outcome locally and never resends

Ok.description: Successful local-only mutation with no richer result

ActionStatus.description: Status of a queued action transmission. `sent` means reserved for a socket write (marked before the write so a cut never resends it); whether it reached the socket is unknown until `ok`/`error` arrives.

kind.description: Kind of saved observation; does not grant native receipt_user membership.

server.description: Serialized Server enum, not wire domain text.

contact.description: Actual serialized ContactId/Jid object; CLI input JID strings use the separate Jid schema.

device.description: Device attribution where applicable; null for a server ACK. Direct participant-qualified receipts preserve this actual actor only when its user matches the saved direct chat and its device belongs to the immutable original target snapshot. Authenticated PN/LID association may join namespaces; historical target gaps are not filled from current membership.

server_timestamp.description: Parsed server ACK or supported receipt time in milliseconds, separate from local observed_at. APK 37.71 signed BMP-decimal parsing and wrapping multiplication apply. Success ACK missing/invalid t defaults to zero (1Qy.A02); direct/group receipt facts retain valid supplied root t, including signed zero/negative/wrapped values, and omit missing/nontext/invalid time (Cmk.A03/0Gv.A01). Receipt facts preserve the first observation per kind/device; later earliest-positive device-row times can differ. Historical facts remain unmodified. This is evidence, not clock authority, native receipt_user admission or completed delivery. Offline tested; qualifying live receipt projection unverified. Offline aggregated message_id receipt facts instead require each entry t via strict Java-decimal parsing; missing/invalid input refuses the entire batch. Valid signed/wrapped values remain supplied evidence; no wall-clock fallback is used for this branch. Participants-key multi-target receipts instead apply root status and each target time; absent entry t uses one confirmed/local receipt-parser clock default. Present malformed/overflow time refuses the entire batch, and missing/invalid optional JIDs skip before time parsing. Native NTP preference is unported; this fallback can differ from the APK when NTP is active. It is not new clock authority.

DeliveryFact.description: Actual serialized durable DeliveryFact; inspect using status.

progress.description: Local attempt progress; delivery evidence is stored separately in facts.

facts.description: Durable facts in local observation order. ServerAccepted is not handset delivery or read.

SendStatus.description: Actual serialized SendStatus returned by CLI status. No HTTP message-status route is served.

wire_id.description: Client-generated wire ID when persisted; null while profile format is unknown.

accepted_at.description: Local durable enqueue time, Unix milliseconds; not server acceptance.

SendTicket.description: Actual serialized ticket for a durable local send intent.

to.description: Direct recipient: E.164 digits, a `…@s.whatsapp.net` JID, or a `…@lid` JID. Omit when `group` is set. The LID form exists because a LID-addressed chat encrypts under a LID Signal address, which needs to be testable outside a group fan-out.

group.description: Group chat JID (`…@g.us`) for a sender-key fan-out send. Mutually exclusive with `to`. lab-transport sends group text, replies and reactions only and refuses group image/voice_note/view_once JSON; outbox-send also accepts uploaded group image/voice_note (2026-10-13: previously the shared reader refused group media, so the documented outbox-send group media path was unreachable from the CLI). lab-transport resolves the membership with a `w:g2` info query, the members' devices with `usync devices`, then addresses every device individually.

fresh_sessions.description: Discard the saved Signal session with each recipient device and establish a new one from a fresh prekey bundle, keeping the pinned peer identity (a changed identity is still refused). Applies to both the direct and the group fan-out path. Only legitimate with positive evidence that the peer never received what was encrypted under the old session.

skdm_delivery.description: Group send only: how the sender key is distributed. `participants` (default) puts one `<enc>` per device inside the group stanza's `<participants>`; `direct` sends one ordinary direct message per device carrying the distribution, before the group stanza, and omits `<participants>` entirely. Both are real — `includeSenderKeysInMessage` is a per-send flag in SendE2EMessageJob and SendLiveLocationKeyJob distributes keys entirely out of band.

image.description: Path to a PNG image file to send

voice_note.description: Path to an Ogg/Opus audio file to send as a voice note

view_once.description: If true, image is sent as view-once (disappears after one viewing)

status.description: Post a status instead of sending to a chat; mutually exclusive with `to` and `group`

quote.description: Reply to, or react to, an existing message in the chat named by `group` or `to`. lab-transport handles group replies (with optional quoted_text) and group reactions, and refuses any direct-chat quote. outbox-send (normal outbox) accepts replies only, in groups and (2026-10-13) direct chats, with exactly one of text, image or voice_note, and refuses reactions and quoted_text before any store access or send-path claim: a participant naming one of our identities quotes our outgoing message; any other names the incoming author, which in a direct chat must be the contact itself in the same form as `to`. quotedMessage is built from the saved parent, never a caller preview.

MessageRequest.description: Private JSON message request for outbox-send or lab-transport --message. Exactly one target: `to` (direct), `group` (sender-key fan-out) or `status` (a status post). Repeating the same request_id returns the saved outcome locally and never resends.

state.description: Current state of the queued entry

OutboxEntry.description: An entry in the durable outbox queue awaiting transmission

kind.description: Type of action (block, report, lookup, etc.)

error_code.description: Server error code if action failed

error_text.description: Server error message if action failed

ActionOutcome.description: Outcome of a one-shot queued action

status.description: Durable receipt transmission outcome. An acknowledged retry is not confirmation of replacement-message delivery.

message_id.description: Wire message ID referenced by the queued receipt; no recipient or message content is included.

ReceiptOutcome.description: Outcome of a queued read, played or automatic once-only retry receipt transmission.

state.description: Saved attempt state name exactly as RegistrationState::name() prints it

blocked_reason.description: Reason for account block if state is blocked. Since 2026-10-13 a saved ServerRefused may carry not_before: the earliest time another request of the refused kind may be sent, the longest sms_wait, voice_wait or email_otp_wait of a refusal without retry_after. The one-shot diagnostics and corrections, resume-email-challenge and the exist probe enforce it. Absent in older records and when the refusal carried no wait.

retry_after_seconds.description: Seconds to wait before retrying if in cooling_down state

RegistrationStep.description: Snapshot of the current registration state and next actions

generation.description: Attempt generation number for state recovery

phone.description: Phone number in masked format (+1 <10 digits>)

RegistrationAttempt.description: Complete registration attempt with full state history

token.description: Base64-encoded phone-bound registration token derived from APK comparison material

signed_pre_key_id.description: Signed pre-key ID (must fit in 24 bits)

facebook_device_id.description: Facebook device identifier; null means generate once and persist

experiment_id.description: Experiment identifier; null means generate once and persist

access_session_id.description: Access session identifier; null means generate once and persist

recovery_token.description: Account recovery token; null means generate once and persist

backup_token.description: Backup recovery token; null means generate once and persist

fields.description: Request field templates organized by step (exist, code, register, security) with optional _bytes variants for encoded versions

body_mode.description: HTTP body encoding mode: clear_form (plaintext form), enc (encrypted), or enc_empty_h (encrypted with empty hash)

connect_timeout_ms.description: TCP connection timeout in milliseconds (must be <= timeout_ms)

max_response_bytes.description: Maximum response body size in bytes

max_attempts.description: Maximum consecutive reconnection attempts (0 disables reconnection). The count resets only after an activated connection stayed up for at least max_delay_ms, or on an explicit connect; a server that activates and then drops at once still exhausts it (client policy, not an APK value).

max_delay_ms.description: Maximum backoff delay in milliseconds; also the minimum activated-connection lifetime that resets the attempt count

action_delay_ms.description: Pause between consecutive queued-action sends in one session

mark_read.description: During a messaging session (`listen`), send a read receipt for every incoming direct or group message with readable content (Message fields 1, 3, 6, 7, 8, 9, 26 or 66) that decrypts. Sender-key distributions, protocol messages and reactions get none. Each receipt goes through the same durable, once-only queue as `mark-read`. Applies to `listen` and to `lab-transport --receive`. Off by default: the official client marks messages read when a chat is on screen, which this client cannot infer. Applies to eligible authenticated duplicates on redelivery too, including offline recovery; durable read markers prevent repetitions after uncertain writes or ACKs.

identity_changes.description: Incoming remote prekey trust policy for listen and lab receive. pinned refuses changed saved identities. apk_authenticated permits replacement only after nested message authentication, atomically archiving the prior pin/session and emitting IdentityChanged with the inbox commit. It does not establish human verification. Own-device messages remain pinned. Outgoing bundle replacement has a separate opt-in outgoing_identity_changes; uncertain sends never replay.

outgoing_identity_changes.description: Independent outgoing remote directory-bundle policy for the normal comparison outbox. Pinned suspends changed identities. Apk_authenticated requires a valid signed device key received through authenticated Noise, derives a fresh peer session, archives prior pin/session with signed_directory_bundle provenance and emits IdentityChanged atomically with the original send reservation. Own-account identities remain pinned. It is not human verification. Incoming identity_changes does not enable this. Unknown/refused queries and uncertain sends never resume. Repeating the original outbox-send JSON may resolve an identity-suspended intent using its saved reply; no new query or intent ID is created. General listen --send-outbox does not select suspended intents. Suspensions without an observed pin snapshot cannot resume, and stale replies cannot roll a newer current peer pin back. This setting applies to direct and ordinary group normal-outbox bundles actually fetched by their workflows. Group replacements archive signed-directory provenance atomically with the original fanout/send reservation and rotate exposed sender-key generations. Own identities remain pinned. A changed primary with companions whose saved authority used its old pin blocks as companion_authority_changed. Group preparation resume and companion reconciliation remain unfinished; no marker is reset and cached sessions do not trigger unsolicited directory refreshes.

A status reaction is an ordinary Message.reactionMessage (field 46) whose key names status@broadcast as the remoteJid — that is what distinguishes it from a chat reaction. In the APK it lands in status_add_on with type = 1, which a trigger counts into status_interactions.reaction_count.

Null until a parsed bundle, including signature-invalid bundles. This is server input inspected offline, not a local switch or complete native admission.

companion_same_key_authority.description: Local known-companion same-key directory authority diagnostic. Null for primary, incomplete or invalid-signature replies. ready for a listed companion requires a unique nonnull device-identity byte body, exact held companion key, current saved membership bound to its primary pin, protected own namespace and no explicit pending teardown. ADV bytes are not parsed on that listed same-key fast return. This diagnostic does not authorize application: pinned policy, metadata, original guards and atomic reply/session/account checks still apply. Changed companion ADV authority is reported separately in companion_changed_key_authority. ready_addition_pending means an already pinned companion is absent from retained membership and its full signed ADV passes independent-primary/E2EE/raw-ID/index/newer signed-time admission. If application policy/metadata/original guards and exact transaction state still permit it, membership plus ADV provenance, pending sync and session are committed together. A same key does not bypass ADV parsing while absent. Index collision, 1024-device overflow or explicit pending teardown refuse. No first-seen pin, invented removal state or canonical PN/LID alias is authorized.

companion_changed_key_authority.description: Local changed-companion directory authority diagnostic. Null for primary, incomplete/invalid-signature replies or when no differing held pin exists. Requires independently pinned primary, current bound device-list baseline, both ADV signatures over the actual directory identity, E2EE/raw-ID baseline and signed Java-long freshness. ready_refresh_pending raises the pending expectation atomically with application, retaining the verified floor and existing device index. ready is not permission to bypass identity policy, original notification guards, unsupported metadata, own identity or exact commit-state checks. First-seen companions, primary/raw-ID replacement and full native admission remain unported. ready_addition_pending means an already pinned companion is absent from retained membership and its full signed ADV passes independent-primary/E2EE/raw-ID/index/newer signed-time admission. If application policy/metadata/original guards and exact transaction state still permit it, membership plus ADV provenance, pending sync and session are committed together. A same key does not bypass ADV parsing while absent. Index collision, 1024-device overflow or explicit pending teardown refuse. No first-seen pin, invented removal state or canonical PN/LID alias is authorized.

identity_auth.description: Content-free selected-user identity_auth shape, or null when absent/unavailable. The classic prekey signature_valid field does not verify identity_auth certificates or signature. Certificate/signature verification remains unported. Structurally valid identity_auth is log-only metadata; malformed required fields defer classic refresh.

IdentityNotificationSessionPreview.description: Redacted offline session candidate diagnostics. This is neither native admission nor a committed refresh.

outcome.description: Fixed preparation result or reason no candidate was derived; errors are separate redacted local refusals.

held_session.description: A serialized session was present in the single read snapshot; presence alone does not prove validity.

archived_states.description: Number of archived states in the discarded candidate; null when derivation is skipped. Supported changed-key candidates are fresh with zero old archives; same-key candidates archive the held receiving state.

admission_evaluated.description: Always false: native CPB attestation/property/stored-state policy is unported.

persisted.description: Always false: candidate bytes are discarded, not exported or written.

PeerAttestationInspection.description: APK-derived non-E2EE attestation verification, separate from native CPB acceptance and trust.

status.description: Fixed redacted local verification status. Ambiguous nodes and the 64 KiB payload bound are local guards; no server refusal is inferred.

declared_account_type.description: Recognized stanza account_type, never arbitrary returned text; null if absent, unsupported or not evaluated.

payload_account_type.description: BP2 closed protobuf enum projection: default E2EE=0, hybrid=1, non-E2EE=2. These differ from C0F stored-state values. null if parsing was not reached or failed.

signature_valid.description: Verification of 06 07 plus original body under the fetched type-5 identity, only after recognized types agree; null before verification. Signature alone is not native admission, directory authentication or human verification.

IdentityAuthInspection.description: Read-only selected directory-user identity_auth shape (APK Bot.A03/CXs). No raw certificates, signatures, keys or IDs. X.509 chain validation and EdDSA verification are unported; effective property 20107 is unknown, with APK modes NONE/LOG_ONLY; presence is not validity.

version.description: Signed Java-decimal version; missing/invalid/out-of-int32 input reports -1, matching 0Gv.A00 default. Version 1 alone does not imply validity.

certificate_count.description: Number of cert children under selected certs child; other extensions ignored.

certificate_bytes_present.description: A nonempty certificate list where every cert has a byte body. Empty byte bodies count as present and are not validated.

signature_bytes_present.description: Selected signature child has a byte body; even empty bytes are presence, not validity.

verification.description: No certificate or identity-auth signature verification is performed by this shape inspection.

capture.description: inbound-undecodable:sha256:<digest of the decrypted frame>; a digest, not content or an address.

class.description: Fixed decoder error class when captured (CodecError::class).

epoch.description: Actor-local connection epoch that captured the frame; null when a lab-transport window captured it.

current_class.description: Error class from the current decoder, or null when it now decodes (for example after a dictionary update). Nothing is reprocessed.

after_cursor.description: The consumer's acknowledged cursor; the batch starts after it.

ack_cursor.description: Cursor that `events --ack` would acknowledge for this batch (equal to after_cursor when it is empty).

has_more.description: More events exist beyond the 50-event batch.

kinds.description: SyncEvent::kind names in journal order. As of 2026-10-13 the set is new_message, message_updated, message_deleted, receipt_updated, send_status_changed, group_created, group_updated, identity_changed, history_gap, group_history_notice, unsupported_message, session_revoked and chat_cleared; SyncEvent::kind in crates/whatsapp-api/src/sync.rs is authoritative.
