get.summary: Show queued one-shot actions and their outcomes
get.description: Show queued one-shot actions (block list, reports, lookups) and their outcomes (offline, redacted). Includes identity_refresh directory reads queued by authenticated identity notifications. An ok action means a correlated generic result, not verified bundle or adopted identity. Refused/invalid/uncertain reads are retained; offline inspection never transmits a chat or changes a pin/session. For identity_refresh actions only, --show prints a structured redacted snapshot with namespace/device, exact refusal code, signed-bundle validity and current-pin comparison; no raw request, reply, peer address or key is printed. verified_bundle authenticates the fetched signed device key, not adoption or human verification. --show ID --preview-session is an offline cryptographic preview for identity_refresh only. It derives and discards a supported primary or authenticated companion classic session without constructing a chat. Same-key candidates retain held receiving state in the candidate archive; changed keys derive fresh with zero old archives. It never writes a candidate or evaluates native CPB admission. Unsupported attestation, PQ metadata, missing pins, unverified replies and failed companion authority do not derive; a reused held session that does not deserialize or whose remote identity, local identity or registration does not match the pin and saved account reports held_session_inconsistent; application defers with the same reason (row kept, logged), so connection-start recovery never stops on it. Evidence docs/protocol/hybrid-identity-refresh.md#damaged-held-sessions-2026-10-13. Unknown native stored attestation state is not assumed NOT_SET or E2EE. Evidence: docs/protocol/session-refresh-preview.md. Newly queued identity_refresh actions now atomically capture original generation, exact pin fingerprint, exact-device authenticated transition marker and nullable primary-user version. --show prints refresh_guard (matches, untracked, pin_changed, transition_changed, primary_version_changed, generation_changed); markers and fingerprints stay private. Duplicate events keep the original baseline; missing historical snapshots remain untracked. Matching guards do not establish CPB admission or commit authority. --preview-session skips derivation for a known stale guard. Evidence: docs/protocol/identity-refresh-guards.md. For supported selected-device identity_refresh replies, --show additionally inspects non_e2ee_attestation: allowed declared account type, BP2 field-1 closed-enum projection, matching type and signature over APK prefix 06 07 plus the original value bytes. Attestation and signed-key validity remain separate from current-pin agreement, refresh guards and native CPB admission. Raw values/signatures and unknown server strings are never printed. Absent, malformed, oversized, mismatched and invalid-signature results are local inspector statuses, not server response codes. Native stored-state/property transitions remain unported; primary branch invariants now permit the application described below. Evidence: docs/protocol/attestation-verification.md. With transport.identity_changes=apk_authenticated, the actor now applies a correlated verified changed-primary classic identity_refresh reply when its original notification guard still matches. Present non_e2ee_attestation or pqkey metadata and companion candidates and same-key candidates without a selected-user force_override_e2ee_state child remain deferred. The APK CPB plain changed-key branch admits under both main-property values; native stored attestation state/effective properties remain unknown and are not synthesized. Pin, fresh session, encrypted old-state archive, transition invalidation and once-only application marker commit atomically after reply/account/guard/session/own PN-LID rechecks. Startup repairs a cut after settlement without replaying IQs. --show reports applied as a historical fact; pin_matches and refresh_guard describe current state. No chat or identity-notification ACK is created. Evidence: docs/protocol/identity-refresh-application.md. Identity refresh inspection includes nullable force_override_e2ee_state from the correlated selected-user child; presence is separate from signature/admission/guard/application. See docs/protocol/same-key-refresh.md. Identity refresh inspection now includes nullable identity_auth metadata shape: effective int32 version, certificate count, byte-body presence and explicit unported verification. This reports no raw certificates/signatures and is separate from classic signed-prekey signature_valid; structurally valid identity_auth does not gate classic adoption; malformed required fields defer. See docs/protocol/identity-auth.md. Identity-auth admission correction (APK 37.71): NONE/LOG_ONLY modes and failure logging do not gate classic session processing. A present selected-user identity_auth requires a signature byte body and certs node; otherwise malformed_identity_auth defers application and preview. Structurally valid metadata preserves existing classic signature/policy/original-guard/ADV checks and does not assert certificate trust. Inspection verification remains unported. Offline tested; fresh live metadata application unverified. Evidence docs/protocol/identity-auth.md. Primary attestation admission (APK 37.71): under the existing apk_authenticated policy and original classic-bundle/account/pin/session guards, structurally valid changed-primary metadata follows the native E2EE fallback even when attestation verification fails; verified same-key hybrid/non-E2EE metadata permits session refresh without force_override_e2ee_state. Missing/non-byte/ambiguous required metadata, failed same-key verification, PQ and companion attestation remain deferred. Inspection preserves its actual verification status. Primary read-only preview may prepare a verified matching-key session and a fresh changed-key candidate through supported metadata fallback; admission_evaluated and persisted remain false. Preview does not grant policy approval, adopt a key, evaluate full native admission or send a request. See docs/protocol/session-refresh-preview.md. Native C0F persistence, effective MobileConfig and non-E2EE send routing remain unported. Offline tested; fresh live attestation application unverified. Evidence docs/protocol/primary-attestation-admission.md. Companion attestation admission (APK 37.71): structurally valid selected-user non_e2ee_attestation metadata does not invoke primary CPB policy for a companion. Under apk_authenticated, exact known-device same-key refresh and independently signed ADV changed-key/returning-device admission proceed through their existing guards even when attestation verification fails. Required byte bodies and local duplicate ambiguity guards still apply. Inspection retains the actual failed/null verification status; application never upgrades it to attestation trust. PQ, malformed identity_auth, stale guards, own identities, missing/invalid ADV and pinned-policy key changes remain refused. Companion preview now uses the existing directory ADV/membership checks and derives a discarded same-key or changed-key candidate; it writes nothing. See docs/protocol/companion-attestation-admission.md#companion-session-preview--2026-10-11. Native attestation state/non-E2EE routing and fresh live application remain unported/unverified. Evidence docs/protocol/companion-attestation-admission.md. Optional receipt-address correction (APK 37.71): direct/group fact routing now shares nullable namespace admission with receipt ACK construction. Namespace-invalid optional recipient/participant fields follow the native null path; mere raw attribute presence no longer hides a matching supported fact. Recognized qualifiers retain their route restrictions, group participants remain required, and original chat/message-ID/addressed-device/authenticated-mapping guards still apply. Raw capture, independent delivery/read/played observations, outbox attempts, read policy, request IDs, keys and waits are preserved. Full specialized JID subtype casts, self-status processing and fresh live fact projection remain unported/unverified. Evidence docs/protocol/receipt-optional-addresses.md. --preview-session also supports authenticated companion same-key and changed-key candidates, including returning-device authority, using one saved read snapshot. Same-key candidates archive the held receiving state; changed keys derive fresh. No list addition, pending refresh, pin/session write or network action occurs. Concrete companion refusals are exposed through outcome; persisted and admission_evaluated remain false. This supersedes earlier primary-only preview descriptions. Evidence docs/protocol/companion-attestation-admission.md#companion-session-preview--2026-10-11. PQ signature diagnostic (APK 2.26.37.71): selected identity refresh metadata now exposes nullable pq_signature with signature-only status, original value byte count, nullable signature_valid and key_validation=unported. It verifies unchanged pqkey/value bytes under the returned candidate identity without an EC prefix, using the existing Signal signature primitive. Classic signature reporting stays independent. A verified signature does not validate KEM format/algorithm or authorize derivation/adoption; existing PQ guard and preview/application deferral remain active. No raw key/signature/ID or saved state is exposed or changed, and no live request runs. Evidence docs/protocol/pq-signature.md. Hybrid identity refresh (2026-10-13, offline): for primary PN/LID peers, a selected pqkey whose signature over the original value bytes and ML-KEM-1024 encoding verify no longer defers as pq_session_unported. --preview-session reports prepared with zero (changed) or one (same-key) archived state, and application commits a version-4 candidate through the same guarded transaction (changed keys fresh; same-key only under the existing force_override_e2ee_state admission, archiving held state). Invalid PQ material defers as pq_bundle_invalid; companion and attestation-bearing PQ remain pq_session_unported. pq_signature.key_validation is now not_checked, valid_ml_kem_1024 or invalid_ml_kem_1024 (formerly always unported); a valid encoding is not trust or adoption. No live PQ refresh is verified. Evidence docs/protocol/hybrid-identity-refresh.md. HTTP (2026-10-13): served read-only by `whatsapp-cli serve --store-routes --token-file <new path>` (experimental-transport build), loopback only, with `Authorization: Bearer <token>`; the store is opened per request with the serve process's --store/--account/--key-env, so it answers 503 store_unavailable only while another command (for example listen) holds the store, and 500 store_read_failed for any other read failure; a command starting during a request can fail to open the store and must be rerun. HEAD is also served. The parameters listed here are CLI flags; over HTTP the store comes from the serve process. peer_ticket is an unsalted address hash (guessable for phone numbers); treat responses as account data. Same library call and redacted JSON as the CLI. Disabled store routes answer 404 store_routes_disabled; a missing or wrong token 401 with WWW-Authenticate: Bearer; any query string 400 (CLI-only options are not served). Over HTTP only the list form is served; --show and --preview-session remain CLI-only.

get.summary: Inspect one saved device query offline
get.description: Offline counts/status inspection; no HTTP handler, account login, query reservation, reset or transmission. Required --id is the existing opaque IQ query ID from the group-send batch log. Unknown IDs return found=false. Found records expose status (outcome_unknown/server_acknowledged/refused), requested_users, ingested distinct users, partial_errors distinct users, omitted_users (nullable historical/unsettled unknown), and a bounded numeric code or null; user addresses and raw response text are never emitted. Omitted means no recognized requested user row in the reply, not a diagnosis of the server internals. A matching result does not prove complete lists. begin_query_for_users validates a selected pending batch of at most 64 input entries, normalizes/deduplicates user addresses, and reserves it atomically; unrelated pending contacts are excluded. Group/status send preparation uses a fixed recipient snapshot, each batch once with message context; require_complete refuses top-level refusal, per-user error or omitted requested users before advancing/reserving a message. Cached lists never bypass this guard. Successful lists and earlier complete batches remain saved; pending omitted/errored users and refused/unknown reservations remain intact. Duplicate rows cannot inflate distinct-user success to hide an omission. Historical QueryRecord rows retain omitted_users=null through serde default without identity/store migration. Background receive synchronization retains partial-success behavior but logs accepted/omitted counts. These are local batching/completeness safeguards over the APK 37.71 usync v2 request/response shape, not inferred server limits, automatic refusal retries or full own-account synchronization. Live 2026-10-07: one existing-peer read in a 20-second receive-only session saved server_acknowledged, one requested/ingested, zero errors/omissions and no code; pending users returned to zero. This validates shared one-user accounting, not selected multi-batch or group-send parity. Primary-only/no signed index list, companions unverified; no chat sends or action/receipt status changes. Default warn/incoming-only logging hides connection INFO counters; saved inspection works independently of log filters. Evidence docs/protocol/messaging-transport.md#scoped-device-batches-and-completeness-2026-10-07. Local durable pending generations now prevent older replies from deleting newer work. QueryRecord.generations is a nullable private aligned vector; superseded_users is nullable and exposed in this offline summary. Neither is a server field or identity. require_complete also refuses superseded users. Background DeviceSyncCursor advances eligible batches, at most 64 per query, once per unchanged revision per connection; refused, errored, omitted or unanswered users remain deferred even after a new notification in that connection. Other users can advance. Contact pending work commits before notification ACK writing, preserving work on an ACK socket cut. Reconciled old replies may update stored lists but retain newer pending revisions. Historical generations/superseded remain null; legacy pending markers default generation zero. Counters survive marker deletion. No new HTTP route, retry/reset switch or chat-send authority. Notification-ID deduplication and own-account/LID sync remain unfinished. Evidence docs/protocol/messaging-transport.md#background-device-revisions-and-continuation-2026-10-07. Live follow-up 2026-10-07 21:57:48 UTC exercised the new cursor in one 20-second receive-only session: one requested/ingested, zero errors/omissions/superseded, code null, pending returned to zero. Outbox/actions/nine acknowledged receipts unchanged; no chat sends. Retained primary only, companions unverified. Live race/large-batch/ACK-cut/timeout coverage remains unknown. Local candidate retention now refuses unsigned non-hosted companions, malformed/missing signed body or timestamp, missing independent primary pin, stale timestamp, invalid signature/protobuf or unsupported different bundled key, raw-ID mismatch and reconciliation failure without replacing cached lists or clearing pending work. DeviceVerificationFailure names fixed local reasons; QueryRecord.verification_failures is nullable and privately durable. device-query exports nullable verification_errors and verification_failures counts; old/unsettled rows remain null. partial_errors remains actual server per-user errors; status server_acknowledged means IQ result even when verification_errors>0, never local completeness. require_complete blocks local refusal before send preparation, including when old cached lists exist. The receive cursor defers rejected users but lets other users progress. Unsigned primary-only reads remain supported. No peer identity, session or own-account state is reset or replaced by this correction. Raw-ID retention is local policy stronger than APK reset behavior, not complete raw-ID replacement support. Full supplied-key application, age-flag parity and authority binding after a changed pin remain unfinished. Evidence docs/protocol/cross-device-sync.md#rejected-device-candidate-retention-2026-10-07. Before mutation, exact duplicate requested-user rows are collapsed; differing rows for the same user refuse with conflicting_user_rows while preserving the cached list/pending revision regardless of row order. This is a local ambiguity guard; APK duplicate dispatch is not established. Background local verification refusal emits a WARN visible under the default log filter, with only the matching opaque local query ID and refusal count so the offline inspector can be invoked; it emits no address/key/body. Inspector output itself still omits the supplied ID. Live 2026-10-07 22:13:51 UTC one-peer 20-second receive-only read completed server_acknowledged, requested/ingested=1, all error/omission/superseded counts zero, verification_failures empty, code null. Pending returned to zero, outbox/actions/nine ACKed receipts unchanged, no chat sends. This validates supported unsigned-primary live behavior and new counts, not live rejected-list or supplied-key replacement.

get.summary: Event kinds after a consumer's acknowledged cursor (offline, redacted)
get.description: The `events --summary --json` form: one object with the consumer name, the acknowledged cursor the batch starts after (after_cursor), the cursor that would acknowledge it (ack_cursor), has_more, and the event kinds in journal order (for example new_message, receipt_updated, message_deleted). No message content, chat, sender or message ID. Reading never acknowledges, so repeating it answers the same batch; acknowledging stays CLI-only (`events --ack`). Without --json the CLI prints one `event: <kind>` line per event and the counts on stderr. A consumer whose cursor precedes trimmed events (for example a name never used before a trim) is refused: the CLI reports the expired cursor, HTTP answers 409 cursor_expired naming the last trimmed cursor (events through it were removed; the first retained event is the next cursor). HTTP (2026-10-13): served read-only by `whatsapp-cli serve --store-routes --token-file <new path>` (experimental-transport build), loopback only, with `Authorization: Bearer <token>`; the store is opened per request with the serve process's --store/--account/--key-env, so it answers 503 store_unavailable only while another command (for example listen) holds the store, and 500 store_read_failed for any other read failure; a command starting during a request can fail to open the store and must be rerun. HEAD is also served. Disabled store routes answer 404 store_routes_disabled; a missing or wrong token 401 with WWW-Authenticate: Bearer. Over HTTP the limit is fixed at the CLI default (50) and the only accepted query is exactly consumer=<name>, unencoded, ASCII alphanumerics and -_.: only, at most 64 bytes (the library ConsumerId bound); a missing, renamed, repeated, empty, percent-encoded or additional parameter (including limit) answers 400 before the store opens. A consumer name using other printable characters, which the CLI accepts, cannot be queried over HTTP. The other parameters listed here are CLI flags; over HTTP the store comes from the serve process.

Supported history-notice metadata is validated using BX5 and DA8.CF4: history receivers, positive oldest-window timestamp and positive message count are required. Local diagnostic limits are 65536 bytes and 1024 entries per receiver list, not server requirements. Context and bot bodies are opaque and not validated. This metadata check does not implement group/app-data dispatch, authorization or rendering. Metadata values remain redacted; history is not fetched or applied. Poll inspection reports question/option byte lengths and counts, selectable count and secret-presence; it no longer prints question or option text. Unknown nested fields remain visible, and malformed nested protobuf fails inspection. This label does not establish sender authorization, history availability, or synchronization completion. With `inspect: true`, display the plaintext protobuf structure without advancing sessions. With replay_captures, preserved message captures are re-run through inbox::process offline to recover stanzas that an earlier defect refused; this is how the first live group messages were recovered after the sender-key distribution field number was corrected. With --inspect, prekey_pin_matches compares the first pkmsg public identity to saved comparison-direct pins for from, sender_pn, participant and participant_pn aliases. Some(true) means matching, Some(false) means differing, None means no saved pin; invalid_input marks malformed inspection data, and invalid_ciphertext marks a non-byte pkmsg payload. This is offline, read-only, prints no keys or full addresses, does not authenticate the ciphertext and does not authorize a pin replacement. Signal failures report fixed redacted categories rather than underlying address/backend strings. --accept-authenticated-identity-changes requires --replay-captures and conflicts with --inspect. It explicitly selects APK-compatible incoming remote key changes after successful authentication. Previous pins/sessions are archived, an IdentityChanged event is emitted atomically with the inbox/session/prekey commit, and no receipt or network request is sent. Default remains pinned. This is not human verification; no safety-number algorithm is claimed. Group pairwise Signal children from a LID participant select the held LID session; participant_pn identifies a contact alias and does not displace that ratchet. A mapped new pkmsg establishes a LID session; msg retains PN fallback when no LID session exists. An unmapped LID may use a held session. Wrong-session correction recovered the remaining original group capture offline in an isolated store, without network requests or changing the original account. Capture shape inspection now recognizes the exact APK 37.71 group notification type w:gp2 despite its digit. Unknown numeric-containing type values remain redacted as none; the general filter is not widened to expose IDs/addresses. Saved group create/groups_dirty structures remain inspection-only; this label does not apply membership, acknowledge notifications or fetch groups. Newly authenticated SKDM-only group controls use private sender_key_distributed markers without user protobuf; inspection labels the committed key distribution without values or read receipts. It does not parse missing user plaintext, synthesize historical markers or rewind ratchets. These controls dedupe as Duplicate; no new HTTP route is added. Status is signatures_verified, missing_device_identity, missing_primary_pin, invalid_primary_pin, ambiguous_input, unsupported_sender, invalid_input or invalid; invalid includes a fixed companion_adv_reason without addresses, keys, ciphertext or ADV bytes. Primary sender paths add no companion result. The primary pin is read only in the actual sender namespace; no alias or companion pin substitutes. Both account and device signatures bind exact signed details and the ciphertext identity, with APK 37.71 E2EE/HOSTED prefixes selected by device type. A supplied account key must match the existing independent pin. inspect.description: Inspect saved plaintext protobuf structure without advancing sessions. Also prints, per preserved capture, the stanza tag/type, attribute names, enc child v/type values, and how the receive path would route it (from/participant server kinds and whether it routes as a group). Also prints the per-class counts on offline/offline_preview stanzas (message, receipt, status, notification, appdata, call), which is how to tell whether the server ever queued a given class of stanza for this account at all.

replay_captures.description: Re-run preserved incoming message captures through the normal receive path, offline. The server delivers a queued stanza once, so a stanza refused by a since-fixed guard is only recoverable from its capture. Already-committed messages dedupe; nothing is transmitted and no receipt is sent.

Later on 2026-11-01: the normal outbox no longer blocks such a reaction; it sends each missing distribution first as a direct message, waits for each server ACK, then sends the reaction without participants (offline-tested; the shape was decrypted live only by our own receiving client, not a handset, and the one handset test of out-of-band distribution on 2026-09-22 failed unexplained). A refused distribution blocks as distribution_refused with the reaction reserved but unsent (uncertain); reaction_distribution_unsupported remains only on older saved preparations.

A caller-provided MessageRef alone cannot attribute another saved chat's body. Foreign originals refuse locally with saved quoted message belongs to another chat, before login-identity writes; ambiguous wire IDs refuse rather than choosing the first record. Unknown IDs retain the existing empty-quote fallback. These are local attribution guards, not new server refusal reasons or retry authority. Unknown targets carry an empty text preview. Default request-ID recipes remain unchanged. Group reactions preserve the original chat and participant, including removal, and use add_on/decrypt-fail metadata. A late changed target is blocked as reference_changed without a wire attempt or query replay. This is a CLI-only queue operation, with no HTTP route or live group validation. Private MessageRequest quote stays on the comparison JSON path. Evidence docs/protocol/normal-group-outbox.md#typed-group-quotes-and-reactions-2026-10-09. Agent components cannot be represented by the current MessageRef and refuse explicitly; hosted/agent reference parity remains unfinished. 2026-10-13: quoted media is now sendable through the library (MessageContent::Media with quoted, uploaded image or voice note, direct and normal group outbox) and through outbox-send group JSON replies; this reply command stays text-only. The quote uses the same participant/quotedMessage rules as text, placed in the media message's contextInfo (field 17). No live quoted media send has been made. Evidence docs/protocol/quoted-media.md#sending-2026-10-13.

post.description: Queue a vote on an existing poll. The operation is offline and returns immediately with a send ticket; a later session transmits it. Omit options to retract the vote. Own poll votes now bind the saved poll-secret chat to the actual primary voter using exact PN/LID address identity or one existing authenticated-lid association; contact/directory aliases and raw sender_pn alone cannot attribute the poll. Successful AEAD projection preserves the original saved chat and actual voter, without changing send outcomes or projection markers. Missing legacy chat binding or unrelated/unsupported routes stay opaque; malformed saved bindings/maps refuse with fixed local diagnoses. Outgoing vote preparation additionally checks the actual saved chat before reading identity or generating entropy, reporting saved poll has no chat binding, invalid saved poll chat binding, or saved poll belongs to another chat. Queuing a vote remains offline; these checks occur when preparing it for transport. lab-inbox --inspect adds a redacted own poll stored-selector binding label: matched, unattributed, missing_chat_binding, unknown_poll, inspection_failed or invalid_peer. Foreign, cleared, missing or ambiguous parents refuse; existing local reservations remain unchanged and authoritative. No cache import, lookup state mutation or automatic vote. Evidence docs/protocol/synchronized-poll-secret.md. Original wrapper, account/pin/session guards, atomic receive commit, sender confirmation and reopen deduplication remain effective. Foreign voters, missing/ambiguous/cleared or special parents, participant/group/status/device keys, mixed content and nonempty edited metadata refuse without a ratchet commit. No new intent, send-status fact, automatic read or retry reservation. This supersedes earlier blanket own-device vote-update limitations. Full edit/special/native parent policy and fresh live interoperability remain unfinished. Evidence docs/protocol/own-device-vote.md.

post.summary: One comparison-server connection; optional bounded primary login
post.description: Establish a single connection to the comparison server (x-live) with optional bounded primary login, message transmission, or receive mode. A successful login records this account's own LID from the `<success>` stanza, which a LID-addressed group names us by. When the message JSON carries `group` instead of `to`, the send is a sender-key fan-out: a `w:g2` info query resolves the membership, a `usync devices` query resolves each member's devices, `encrypt` supplies bundles for devices without a session, and one `<message>` carries a per-device `<enc>` distribution inside `<participants>` beside the group `skmsg`. It refuses rather than sending when a member has no device list. After any send the connection is held briefly and whatever the server sends next is preserved, because a recipient that cannot decrypt answers with a `receipt type="retry"` naming the failing device. A `<success>` or `<failure>` login result is preserved too: a `<failure>` carries an `appeal_token` and a refusal cannot be replayed to fetch one again. Receive mode shares listen’s durable once-only decryption-failure retry queue; no repeated count=1 requests after redelivery or uncertain writes. Inspect with receipts (offline). Group pairwise Signal children from a LID participant select the held LID session; participant_pn identifies a contact alias and does not displace that ratchet. A mapped new pkmsg establishes a LID session; msg retains PN fallback when no LID session exists. An unmapped LID may use a held session. Wrong-session correction recovered the remaining original group capture offline in an isolated store, without network requests or changing the original account. When mark_read is enabled, eligible authenticated duplicates recovered offline also enter the once-only read queue on redelivery. The helper checks the saved decrypted readable payload; cleared/consumed rows and protocol-only content are skipped. A write-cut regression verifies uncertain reads are never replayed. Newly reserved comparison group/status sends record exact own sender-key exposure atomically with send/session state. After a supported authenticated remote primary change, indexed own keys rotate on the next new intent, with stale-snapshot checks and encrypted prior-key archival. No acknowledged, refused or uncertain intent is replayed; unindexed historical exposure is unknown and full APK bucket/alias/companion parity remains unfinished. Evidence docs/protocol/cross-device-sync.md#durable-own-sender-key-exposure-and-rotation-2026-10-07. Shared directory bundle parsing now requires one exact user/server/agent/device match, ignores only wire-encoding kind, rejects duplicate requested-user rows or optional one-time keys and contradictory outer errors, while allowing other devices in a batch. These are local ambiguity guards; APK duplicate-reply policy remains unknown. Parsing failure never authorizes pin/session mutation, replay or query reset; peer-keys inspection reports existing invalid_reply. Evidence docs/protocol/peer-identity.md#exact-directory-bundle-selection-2026-10-07. Comparison group sends validate saved membership with offline group_send::recipients_for_group before reserving device-list synchronization: mixed namespaces, wrong own form and absent own membership refuse instead of falling back to raw targets. Initial missing device lists are allowed for this validation; own primary is excluded and remote targets are sorted/deduplicated. The final plan still validates list ownership/companion authority before message reservation. This fixes local routing consistency, not complete APK cached mode/category parity or automatic own-PN selection. No new flag, wire attribute or HTTP route exists; actual live PN send remains unverified. Evidence docs/protocol/groups.md#group-recipient-validation-before-device-sync-2026-10-07. Group/status companion version-2 pkmsg now supports the APK 37.71 matched-baseline E2EE branch: both ADV signatures bind the ciphertext identity to an independently held primary; a current independently bound account baseline must have matching raw ID and a verified list timestamp. Old/equal candidates require the actual companion index to match; newer eligible candidates queue expected-timestamp refresh after authentication and may add an absent non-offline device. login.description: Send one primary login after certificate verification

receive.description: Preserve incoming stanzas for up to 30 seconds without sending a chat. Incoming `presence` and `chatstate` stanzas are reported (redacted) as they arrive.

media_route.description: Obtain and privately preserve one current media-upload route response

message.description: Private JSON: request_id, either to (direct) or group (`…@g.us` fan-out), and text, image (PNG) or voice_note (Ogg/Opus); a group send is text only so far

recheck_refusal.description: Authorize exactly one further login after a saved `failure`, to tell a temporary limit from a permanent refusal. Requires a saved `failure` (never an ambiguous `outcome_unknown`), refuses to carry a message, and preserves the earlier refusal under its own key instead of overwriting it.

push_name.description: Set the display name others see beside this number: one `<presence name=… type="available"/>` after login (comparison 2.26.37.71 `LX/0y0->A00`, `WriterThread/write/push-name`, confirmed). Fire-and-forget: the server sends no reply, so the CLI reports `written`, not accepted, and records it under the `push-name` checkpoint. The 100-character bound is this client's; the APK enforces none on the wire. Not live-verified yet.

typing.description: Show a typing indicator in this chat (E.164 digits, a phone/LID JID or a `…@g.us` group): announces `presence type=available`, writes `<chatstate to=…><composing/></chatstate>` (`LX/B2G->A01`, confirmed), holds for `typing_seconds` without reading (a cancelled read closes this channel), then writes `<paused/>` (`LX/B2H->handleMessage`, confirmed). Combined with `message`, the indicator runs before the send. Not live-verified yet.

typing_state.description: `recording` is `composing media="audio"` (shown while recording a voice note); `paused` writes only the stop.

subscribe.description: During `receive`, subscribe to these people's availability and typing, as opening their chat does: after activation, `presence type=available`, then per person `<presence type="subscribe" to=…>` with a `<tctoken>` child carrying their saved trusted-contact token when one is held (comparison 2.26.37.71 `LX/0y0->A00`, `WriterThread/write/subscription-request`, confirmed; token bound 1..=120 bytes). Incoming `presence` (available/unavailable, `last` seen) and `chatstate` (composing/recording/paused) are then reported during the window with identities redacted. People only; group typing arrives without a subscription. Not live-verified yet.

Unknown or category-peer contexts stay opaque; internal APK bypasses and UI feature branches are not enabled. Empty or structured skmsg bodies stay Unsupported even with a stored key, never Decrypted merely because a key exists. Direct/group ciphertext accepts both Bytes and an unchanged UTF-8 Text byte view. This is a local classification/decoder correction; exact APK missing-key retry producers and limits remain unknown. Evidence docs/protocol/messaging-transport.md#missing-group-sender-key-recovery-2026-10-07. SKDM distribution arrives embedded in pkmsg/msg payloads (WhatsApp Message field 2), either standalone or as a second enc child of the group stanza, and is committed atomically with the inbox row. A decrypted group message is confirmed with a receipt addressed to the group carrying the sender as participant. Status updates (from=status@broadcast) route through the same sender-key path and project into a Broadcast chat with the poster as sender, but are never confirmed with a receipt: the status receipt shape (class=status, type=sender) has an unresolved sts input, so none is sent. Each incoming stanza except keepalive replies is reported on stderr as one redacted `incoming` log line (element, type, chat class, enc types, inbox outcome, confirmed, marked_read); this is the default when RUST_LOG is unset. On Undecryptable incoming messages, queues a retry receipt using the saved Signal registration ID. Both listen and lab receive use one request per chat/participant/message ID, durably reserved before transmission; repeats and uncertain outcomes never reset it. This is a conservative client policy, not an APK retry limit. Missing registration or unsupported routing is logged without ending receive; storage failures propagate. The receipts command inspects outcomes offline. Live 2026-10-06: saved-account login and activation succeeded; one automatic retry received a matching server ACK. Its redelivery still failed decryption, and fresh-message automatic read validation remains pending. Signal failure diagnostics classify missing keys, untrusted identity, bad MAC, duplicate counter and invalid encoding without printing peer addresses or backend details. This does not explain the historical window with no incoming message stanzas. Offline preserved-capture inspection found incoming prekey identities differing from both saved PN and LID pins; no pin was replaced. Human safety-number verification is not implemented, and the underlying cause of the saved mismatch remains unknown. Explicit authenticated incoming replacement is available as described below. Direct and group pairwise prekey processing persists first-seen differing public-key fingerprints; identity-conflicts inspects these unauthenticated observations offline. Pins and sessions are not replaced. A failing direct Signal child within a group stanza is also Undecryptable and eligible for the same once-only retry; missing sender-key/session support remains Unsupported. transport.identity_changes explicitly selects pinned (default) or apk_authenticated; the latter atomically archives old remote keys/sessions and emits IdentityChanged after message authentication. Local/own-device identities are not replaced. Group pairwise Signal children from a LID participant select the held LID session; participant_pn identifies a contact alias and does not displace that ratchet. A mapped new pkmsg establishes a LID session; msg retains PN fallback when no LID session exists. An unmapped LID may use a held session. Wrong-session correction recovered the remaining original group capture offline in an isolated store, without network requests or changing the original account. When mark_read is enabled, eligible authenticated duplicates recovered offline also enter the once-only read queue on redelivery. The helper checks the saved decrypted readable payload; cleared/consumed rows and protocol-only content are skipped. A write-cut regression verifies uncertain reads are never replayed. Live 2026-10-07: a 45-second session delivery-confirmed the two recovered direct/group messages as duplicates. A subsequent 20-second session server-acknowledged both explicitly queued saved-message reads; eight reads and one retry are now acknowledged. Handset blue ticks and fresh-message automatic reads remain unconfirmed. Newly settled supported group-action replies now project snapshots/events inside the receive session without requiring group list. Settlement creates a durable pending-projection marker; startup recovers only these newly marked replies and never requeues their requests. Projection and pending-marker removal share the once-only snapshot/event transaction. Truncated or invalid group replies remain encrypted/pending with a secret-free warning and do not stop unrelated receiving; storage errors still stop the session. Shared decode preserves duration, metadata and parent/source guards and original bytes/IDs/waits; encoding and saved state are unchanged. BP2 attestation projection reuses its original wire rules without new admission policy. post.summary: Request a code or resume an existing attempt; no automatic retries
post.description: Initiates or resumes a registration attempt. Requests a verification code via the specified method (sms or voice). Contacts WhatsApp servers. Waits (2026-10-13): on sent, the handle keeps the longer of the method's wait (sms_wait or voice_wait) and retry_after; a refusal that sets a cooldown keeps the longest SMS, voice or (since 2026-10-13) email wait it carries. Not-sent requests (2026-10-13, offline): a request that could not be built (for example a config edited since the attempt froze it) or whose connection failed before any byte was written returns error RequestNotSent and restores the attempt's state before the reservation (a fresh begin returns to unregistered, which the next begin resumes with the same attempt and keys; a resend keeps its pending challenge and method; a submission returns to its challenge; a consent reservation is released; the code-request one-shots, meaning the diagnostics, corrections and resume-preflight, put back the saved request material their reservation replaced, such as a corrected token, and release their latch in the same transaction) instead of recording an unknown outcome. Any other failure may have reached the server and still records outcome_unknown. Review corrections (2026-10-13, offline): once a /v2/exist preflight has been sent in the same step, a later failure records outcome_unknown, never RequestNotSent; the lab transport's own field-patch or encryption failures count as not sent. Evidence docs/protocol/registration-safety-audit.md. Store creation (2026-10-13): begin no longer creates a missing store unless --create-store is given; the refusal names --profile and --create-store. Evidence docs/protocol/registration-safety-audit.md. Store ownership (2026-10-13, review correction): a store records the number it was created for (accounts new and begin --create-store write it). begin on a store that holds no attempt requires that record to name the config's number: an unclaimed store, such as an empty one another command created, needs --create-store, which claims it; another number's store is refused. A store with an attempt is left to the library, which refuses another number's or profile's attempt. Exact restore (2026-10-13, second review): the attempt written back is the exact copy from before the reservation, history included, so a request that never left adds no history and is not counted as a preparation (code_preparation_count, the preflight's client_metrics.attempts). Resume method (2026-10-13): resuming an elapsed cooldown or a first attempt that never left with a method other than the attempt's is refused, naming the saved method; it used to send with the saved method silently.

create_store.description: Create the store if it does not exist (--create-store). accounts new creates its profile's store, so this is only for a profile made before it did. Without it, a missing store is refused, so a forgotten --profile or a mistyped path cannot create a fresh identity for a number that may already have one. It also claims an unclaimed existing store for the config's number; a store claimed for another number is refused.

Review corrections (2026-10-13, offline): once a /v2/exist preflight has been sent in the same step, a later failure records outcome_unknown, never RequestNotSent; the lab transport's own field-patch or encryption failures count as not sent. Exact restore (2026-10-13, second review): the attempt written back is the exact copy from before the reservation, history included, so a request that never left adds no history and is not counted as a preparation (code_preparation_count, the preflight's client_metrics.attempts). Profile (2026-10-13): refused for an attempt created under another profile, so another flow can never answer (or locally block) a pending server challenge.

get.summary: Print table counts, journal head, generation and registration status
get.description: Returns inspection data for the protocol store including table row counts, journal state and current registration status. Also reports checkpoint_kinds: a count of Checkpoints rows per leading key segment (for example inbound, received, app-state-key, login-identity). Checkpoints holds many unrelated record kinds under one table, so a bare row count cannot answer whether a given kind is present; only the structural prefix is shown, never the JID or digest that follows it. Since 2026-10-13 the kind inbound-undecodable counts decrypted frames listen could not decode; each is kept with its fixed error class for later inspection or re-decoding. whatsapp-cli undecodable lists them, re-checked with the current decoder. Served (2026-10-13) as an opt-in store route: serve --store-routes answers GET /v1/store with the same JSON, under the store bearer token. A checkpoint kind is now printed by name only when it is a lowercase record name ([a-z][a-z0-9_-]*, at most 48 bytes, not hex-like); any other leading segment, for example a key without a ':' separator whose whole text is an address or a digest, is counted under other, for the CLI and the route alike.

post.description: Initializes the account protocol store if it does not exist, or verifies that the master key can open it. This operation is idempotent. post.summary: Rotate the master key: re-wrap the data keys under the key found in the given environment variable
post.description: Re-wraps all data encryption keys under a new master key. The old key stops working immediately. Failed commit (2026-10-13): if the rotation's commit itself fails (for example a full disk or a failed fsync), the outcome is unknown and the error is StoreError::RotationOutcomeUnknown: the store may now open only with the new key, so keep both keys until one of them opens it. Errors before the commit (an unreadable new key, entropy failure) leave the old key in force. Evidence docs/protocol/replay-safety-audit.md#disk-full-and-failed-commits-2026-10-13.

post.summary: Onboard a phone number: derive its token, write the private request configuration with the working recipe, generate its master key and profile
post.description: Derives a registration token for the given phone number, generates the master cryptographic key, creates the account profile, and writes a private request configuration with the APK-derived recipe. The token, key and phone are never printed. Files are created with restrictive permissions: 0600 for profile and config files, 0700 for directories. Next step: lab-signup --allow-live-request begin. Since 2026-10-13 it also creates the profile's encrypted store (so lab-signup begin never has to) and refuses a number another saved profile's request JSON already configures: one number keeps one store. Nothing is written when refused. Duplicate check (2026-10-13, review correction): numbers are compared canonically (separators ignored), each saved profile is read on its own so a malformed one hides nothing, every regular *.json file in the account directory's siblings and in the signup-json-* directories beside its parent is also checked (so lab/accounts/* and lab/signup-json-*, any file name; each read through the config size limit; past a fixed file bound the command refuses with a message rather than answering not configured; configs elsewhere are not seen), the canonical number is written, and the new store is claimed for that number. Store file mode (2026-10-13): a newly created store file is 0600 on unix (records were already encrypted; the file followed the umask before); an existing file's mode is not changed.

This is pending work, not currently sendable reservations; transport guards, support and server waits remain separate. Malformed history produces the existing account error result rather than a partial count; inspection never repairs or deletes history. CLI-only, x-live=false; no HTTP route. Evidence docs/protocol/account-status-counts.md. post.summary: Queue a full usync sync of every saved contact (offline; a session transmits it)
post.description: Register this account's address book with the server using the APK's full/interactive usync mode pair (LX/0u7->A06 envelope, LX/0xX mode-context pairing, both confirmed). This differs from contacts check only in mode and context: check sends query/interactive for a single number, which is discovery rather than address-book registration. allow_mutation is deliberately not emitted because what enables it is unknown. Offline: the request is queued on the durable action queue and a later session transmits it. Whether registering contacts affects Status delivery is unknown and untested; see docs/protocol/status.md.

contacts.description: How many saved contacts the sync includes.

post.summary: Queue a read-only app-state fetch for every collection (offline; a session transmits it)
post.description: Ask the server for each app-state collection's snapshot at version 0 (CSe.A00/CSe.A01: <sync data_namespace=3><collection name order version=0 return_snapshot="true"/>). Read-only: no <patch> child is emitted, since CSe.A01 adds it only when a patch argument is present. The reply carries the server's authoritative version per collection, which patch writing needs because patches must be strictly sequential. Live 2026-09-22: accepted, and the reply was an empty <sync/>, confirming this account holds no app state.

post.summary: Queue an app-state contactAction patch publishing every saved contact (offline; a session transmits it)
post.description: Build and queue a SyncdPatch of contactAction SET mutations, one per saved contact, into the critical_unblock_low collection (LX/Azs->A00 routes contactAction there, confirmed — not a 'regular' collection). Index is ["contact", <jid>] and SyncActionData.version is 2, both confirmed from LX/B6M. Mints this device's app-state key if it has none. The <collection version> attribute is the version the client currently holds and is omitted for a never-synced collection (confirmed, CSe.A01 call sites). LIVE STATUS: refused. Two attempts, both answered iq type=error code=400 text=bad-request; the second carried the corrected version semantics. Not iterated further. See docs/protocol/chat-actions.md for the undistinguished candidates.

post.summary: Ask for a new code on the attempt already in progress
post.description: Re-request the verification code for a registration attempt that is already in a pending challenge, because a delivered code expires long before the attempt does. Keeps the attempt id, its identity, its keys and its history; creates no new attempt; honours the challenge handle's retry_after; and refuses any other state except the saved stale refusal described below. This is the official client's resend, not a restart. Not-sent requests (2026-10-13, offline): a request that could not be built (for example a config edited since the attempt froze it) or whose connection failed before any byte was written returns error RequestNotSent and restores the attempt's state before the reservation (a fresh begin returns to unregistered, which the next begin resumes with the same attempt and keys; a resend keeps its pending challenge and method; a submission returns to its challenge; a consent reservation is released; the code-request one-shots, meaning the diagnostics, corrections and resume-preflight, put back the saved request material their reservation replaced, such as a corrected token, and release their latch in the same transaction) instead of recording an unknown outcome. Any other failure may have reached the server and still records outcome_unknown. Review corrections (2026-10-13, offline): once a /v2/exist preflight has been sent in the same step, a later failure records outcome_unknown, never RequestNotSent; the lab transport's own field-patch or encryption failures count as not sent. Evidence docs/protocol/registration-safety-audit.md. Exact restore (2026-10-13, second review): the attempt written back is the exact copy from before the reservation, history included, so a request that never left adds no history and is not counted as a preparation (code_preparation_count, the preflight's client_metrics.attempts). Also accepts an attempt saved as blocked by a /v2/register `stale` (expired code) refusal, honouring its saved wait. Since 2026-11-01 `stale` no longer blocks: verify-code returns to code entry on a new step (2.26.37.71 VerifyPhoneNumber.A5O case 9 forgets the stored code, clears the input and stays on code entry), so a resend follows. Other refusals still refuse. 2026-11-01: `incorrect` and `mismatch` refusals of a code also return to code entry (2.26.37.71 VerifyPhoneNumber.A5O default branch and A1v); a `mismatch` gates the next code for retry_after or 60 s (answer_not_before) without consuming the step, and resend-code accepts attempts saved as blocked by either.

get.summary: List who has received, viewed, played or liked our statuses
get.description: Offline. Lists the recorded status receipts and likes: who reported, for which status, and how far they got (delivered, read, played), plus any reactions. Receipts are kept at the furthest state a viewer reached, so a delivery replayed from an offline queue cannot demote a view. Reading this sends nothing and emits no read receipt. Status likes require the status@broadcast singleton (zero agent/device), rather than any broadcast-domain reaction key. Other broadcasts, malformed keys and companion-suffixed status targets do not become status likes. Static APK 37.71 BoQ.A00/8oR evidence and local limits: docs/protocol/reactions.md. Recording correction (2026-10-13, offline): only the entry-less participants message_id receipt observed live is a status view; from 2026-10-10 until this correction it was refused as an empty aggregate and ended listen, so views received in that window may be missing. An aggregate with entries is a chat receipt, not a view. Evidence docs/protocol/status.md#views-status-receipts-observed-2026-09-24.

post.summary: Set, change or turn off two-step verification
post.description: Queues an `iq xmlns="urn:xmpp:whatsapp:account" type="set"` carrying `<2fa>` with a `<code>` and/or `<email>` child (confirmed from LX/0lo->A06, TwoFactorXmppMethods/sendSetTwoFactorAuth). Each child is included only when supplied, so setting a PIN cannot clear the recovery address as a side effect, and an empty code turns two-step verification off. The PIN is read from redirected stdin, never a command-line argument, and is never echoed or logged. Distinct from `lab-signup verify-pin`, which answers a PIN challenge rather than changing the PIN. post.summary: Queue the display name as the pushNameSetting app-state record
post.description: Queues an app-state patch to `critical_block` carrying one SET mutation: index `["setting_pushName"]`, `SyncActionData.version` 1, value `SyncActionValue{timestamp: 1, pushNameSetting: 7 {name: 1}}` (comparison 2.26.37.71 `LX/B66`, `LX/Azq`, `LX/BZV`, `LX/BQd`, all confirmed). This is how the account's other devices learn the name; other people see it through the separate `<presence name=…>` stanza sent by `lab-transport --push-name`. Builds on the collection state the server last accepted and promotes the new state only once the server accepts it; a 409 conflict is caught up from the returned patches. Offline: a session such as `listen` transmits the queued action. Live 2026-09-25: accepted, `<collection name="critical_block" version="1"/>`. 2026-11-01: also queues the display-name presence (<presence name type=available/>, 2.26.37.71 0y0 case 3), which the next listen sends once after its availability announcement, so other people see the name without a separate lab-transport login.

get.summary: Inspect durable peer identity conflict observations offline
get.description: Lists first-seen SHA-256 public-key fingerprint differences observed in incoming prekey envelopes. These observations are unauthenticated: they do not establish a legitimate identity change, replace a pin, advance a session, clear verification, or authorize sending. The peer address is represented by a local SHA-256 selector. Replay/redelivery of the same peer/pinned/observed combination preserves the original timestamp. HTTP (2026-10-13): served read-only by `whatsapp-cli serve --store-routes --token-file <new path>` (experimental-transport build), loopback only, with `Authorization: Bearer <token>`; the store is opened per request with the serve process's --store/--account/--key-env, so it answers 503 store_unavailable only while another command (for example listen) holds the store, and 500 store_read_failed for any other read failure; a command starting during a request can fail to open the store and must be rerun. HEAD is also served. The parameters listed here are CLI flags; over HTTP the store comes from the serve process. peer_ticket is an unsalted address hash (guessable for phone numbers); treat responses as account data. Same library call and redacted JSON as the CLI. Disabled store routes answer 404 store_routes_disabled; a missing or wrong token 401 with WWW-Authenticate: Bearer; any query string 400 (CLI-only options are not served).

get.summary: Inspect saved peer pins, sessions and retained-device key coverage (offline)
get.description: Reads one logical snapshot without queries, key replacement or sends. Requires a primary phone-number chat JID. Returns hashed peer selectors, diagnostic public-key fingerprints, held-session/pin agreement, and all authenticated primary LID mappings. A qualifying saved incoming transition establishes local provenance only; it is not a WhatsApp safety number or human verification. Store opening can commit engine metadata; protocol records are inspected read-only. No HTTP route is implemented. Also reports nullable retained E2EE device-key coverage in that snapshot: retained/pinned counts, hashed missing-pin selectors, saved signed-list status, skipped-hosted count and notification-hash agreement. A primary-only fallback or fully pinned retained set does not establish complete current APK fingerprint inventory, selected scheme or human verification. Invalid saved pins/device-list consistency are local diagnostics. No safety number is computed. Reports nullable local verification metadata: verified bit, action sequence and identity/pin agreement. This human claim is distinct from authenticated transition provenance. Saved device_key_coverage additionally exposes nullable device_authority (binding_known, primary_pin_present, primary_pin_matches and companions_current), recomputed read-only against the exact current primary namespace pin. Historical companions_verified does not prove current signer authority; the private binding fingerprint is not exported. No PN/LID alias is inferred. post.summary: Compute native fingerprint display from explicit inputs (offline)
post.description: CLI only; no HTTP route. Does not open the account store, fetch keys, compare QR data, select the active APK scheme, or commit human verification. Raw keys are sorted unsigned, serialized with 0x05, concatenated without deduplication and hashed using APK 37.71 native 5200-round identifier-bound SHA-512. Six big-endian five-byte groups yield 30 digits per side, with lexical join to 60. Native-display fixtures use actual ARM64 hash control flow with host-modeled SHA/MCF; whole native display and live comparison are not established. Complete device inventory and scheme selection remain caller responsibilities. Output contains no input identifier or public key. Resource bounds are client policy. See docs/protocol/safety-number.md. V4 QR needs full plain-primary lid_jid matching display_identifier and at least PN or username presence on each side. Optional QR-specific fields are ignored for display-only calculations. V4 local PN is suppressed with a present username; remote PN retained. Version 1 uses H(K,K), not identifier-bound display hash. get.summary: Inspect saved contact-check status without queuing
get.description: Offline read only. Returns status=null if no saved row exists. Does not ingest, queue/reserve/transmit actions, log in, refresh, reset or migrate historical records. JSON exposes recognized contact_type and fixed malformed-type errors; text uses a masked phone and does not display JIDs. This is a CLI contract, no served HTTP handler. Evidence docs/protocol/chat-actions.md#contact-type-and-offline-status-2026-10-08. Contact projection now runs in receive after reply settlement and on session startup, so reading this status no longer requires queuing another contacts check. Status itself remains read only.

post.summary: Repair a missing LID from one saved reply offline
post.description: Bounded local migration for prior zero-component AD_JID rejection, not an APK command or HTTP handler. Requires existing successful contact-check, saved reply, original request phone, consumed marker, exactly one matching valid user/LID and matching retained status fields. Atomic action-history inspection rejects any other check for the same phone, even queued, or another check with unknown request provenance. Does not order historical timestamps or delete ingestion markers. Existing same LID returns repaired=false; conflicting LID, missing prior row/protocol success, ambiguous/mismatched history or prior incomplete repair refuses with a fixed local reason without echoing the ID/phone. Archives the prior status and fills only a missing LID atomically, keeping checked_at and all other fields. No login, query, action replay, pin/alias/session mutation or fresh identity. This is contact metadata, not identity-replacement authority. Evidence docs/protocol/chat-actions.md#live-contact-projection-and-primary-wire-lid-2026-10-08. Observed offline 2026-10-08 on the original live saved reply: first repaired=true, repeat=false, LID present, checked_at/actions/receipts/empty outbox unchanged. No query was repeated. Fixed local diagnostic reasons identify the failed prerequisite: saved_reply_missing, reply_usync_missing, reply_list_missing, action_missing_or_not_contact_check, action_not_successful, original_request_phone_missing, ambiguous_contact_history, ingestion_marker_missing, matching_user_ambiguous, valid_lid_missing, saved_status_missing, saved_status_mismatch, existing_lid_conflict, repair_history_already_exists. These are local guard names, not server refusal codes.

get.summary: Inspect per-device receipts for a saved comparison group send
get.description: Offline, redacted counts from the original saved message request_id. Returns JSON null when no group-send reservation exists. addressed_devices is null when a historical out-of-band wire has no frozen targets. Delivery/read/played counts are independent per actual participant device and never establish every member received the message. Preserves the recognized send outcome; a recipient receipt does not fabricate a server ACK or reset uncertainty. Newly prepared comparison group sends persist recipient_devices alongside their original group wire; older in-band sends derive targets from that wire. Qualified group receipts match group chat, wire ID and an original device, allowing only an existing authenticated PN/LID association with the same device index. Current group member/device directories alone cannot attribute an older send. Foreign, missing participant, self and recipient-qualified routes remain unsupported; corrupt or ambiguous saved data rolls back. Normal-outbox group facts can use an existing original prepared group envelope, but the normal comparison adapter still prepares direct sends only. No group send, replay, mapping adoption or receipt is queued by inspection. Source and live limits: docs/protocol/group-receipts.md. HTTP (2026-10-13): served read-only by `whatsapp-cli serve --store-routes --token-file <new path>` (experimental-transport build), loopback only, with `Authorization: Bearer <token>`; the store is opened per request with the serve process's --store/--account/--key-env, so it answers 503 store_unavailable only while another command (for example listen) holds the store, and 500 store_read_failed for any other read failure; a command starting during a request can fail to open the store and must be rerun. HEAD is also served. Same library call and redacted JSON as the CLI. Disabled store routes answer 404 store_routes_disabled; a missing or wrong token 401 with WWW-Authenticate: Bearer. Over HTTP the store comes from the serve process and the only accepted query is exactly request_id=<id>, unencoded, satisfying the library ID rule (ASCII alphanumerics and -_.:, at most 128 bytes); a missing, renamed, repeated, empty, percent-encoded or additional parameter answers 400 before the store opens. An unknown request_id answers 200 null. The other parameters listed here (store, account, key environment, profile, profiles directory) are CLI flags; over HTTP the store comes from the serve process and any of them is an extra query parameter, answered 400. A damaged saved send, target list or fact row answers 422 saved_state_unsupported with the library's fixed reason (never the group or a device).

get.summary: Inspect frozen directory-key batch outcomes offline
get.description: Read-only directory-key batch counts for an existing private message request_id. Returns null when neither a batch nor a historical key outcome was saved, not a server refusal. Frozen ordinary PN/LID device targets use local 32-device queries, with a local 4096-target bound; neither bound is a claimed WhatsApp server limit. Each next query is durably outcome_unknown before socket write. Unknown/refused/invalid outcomes block without replay; completed replies are reused only for the same normalized frozen device set. An unattributed legacy message:<request_id>:keys row cannot silently start a new batch. Matched IQ result/error replies are preserved encrypted; supported result lists require every exact device once, no foreign/duplicate/omitted targets, well-formed bundles and valid signed-key signatures. Recognized blocking_reason values are local classifications, not detailed server reasons. Raw server text, identifiers, signatures and response wire are not printed. A complete directory lookup does not establish peer trust, send reservation, server message acceptance or delivery. Existing fanout staging still enforces pins. No queries or group/status sends are queued by inspection, and no normal group-outbox adapter is claimed. Evidence docs/protocol/device-key-batches.md. When an old message:<request_id>:keys outcome exists without frozen batch provenance, inspection reports a fixed local error explaining that counts are unknown and the original is preserved; it does not present this as missing server state or invent counts. Hybrid rows (2026-10-13, offline): a selected device row carrying pqkey now answers when its KEM signature over the original value bytes and its ML-KEM-1024 encoding verify; a failed KEM signature is blocking_reason invalid_signature and other PQ defects invalid_bundle. Group/status fan-out then sends that device a native 0x44 hybrid distribution. This client sends no pqsupport attribute; whether the server returns pqkey without it is unknown. Evidence docs/protocol/hybrid-fanout.md. A verified PQ row carrying non_e2ee_attestation or identity_auth without signature bytes and certs is blocking_reason unsupported_bundle (local admission boundary shared with the direct outbox). Evidence docs/protocol/hybrid-fanout.md. HEAD is also served. Same library call and redacted JSON as the CLI. Disabled store routes answer 404 store_routes_disabled; a missing or wrong token 401 with WWW-Authenticate: Bearer. get.summary: Inspect original send-time primary versions (offline, redacted)
get.description: Offline inspection of an existing immutable local outbox intent. Direct and group comparison adapters capture actual target users' nullable primary-device versions in the original send reservation transaction, after authenticated replacement hooks. Group capture includes every planned device, not only newly distributed sender keys. The snapshot is immutable; namespace values stay separate and duplicate device encodings are counted once. Historical/unprepared intents without a snapshot return captured=false and users=[]; captured null counters are known missing values, not missing instrumentation. Each user exports only a normalized-JID hash, device count, at_send/current signed int64-or-null and nullable matches boolean. Equality is diagnostic, never a native resend decision; effective default/hosted gates and full sync/resend runtime remain unported. Unknown local IDs and malformed snapshots/counters refuse with fixed diagnostics; inspection neither repairs history nor sends/queues anything. See docs/protocol/send-version-snapshot.md. New captures retain exact device components; device_targets exposes only component/hash pairs. Old count-only snapshots return null for that field and are never backfilled. Group receipt attribution uses the original full frozen targets when known, requiring original envelope sender-key targets to be a subset. Current fanout still distributes to every target; primary/counterpart cleanup and cached-key distribution omission remain unported. Separate pending device rows are now seeded with original nullable versions in the same reservation transaction. Authenticated, attributed supported root receipts update exact original-device rows with earliest positive server milliseconds (root t parsed as signed ASCII seconds, wrapping multiplication by 1000). Equal/duplicate facts may improve a timestamp without a second fact/event. Historical missing rows remain null; no namespace merging or resend is inferred; authenticated companion deletion is described below. Malformed rows refuse atomically with redacted diagnostics. See docs/protocol/device-receipt-rows.md. Authenticated companion-key replacement now removes only pending exact-device row membership on ordinary direct/group intents. Output present distinguishes removed provenance from a current row; version is current-row nullable version while at_send remains the immutable original. A later supported positive root receipt reinserts a removed original companion row using the current nullable exact-namespace user version. Existing-row timestamp changes preserve version. Both authenticated incoming-message and signed-directory replacement sources share atomic cleanup/history commits. Primary cleanup, counterpart expansion, status/coexistence branches and resend remain unfinished. See docs/protocol/companion-receipt-cleanup.md. Direct supported receipt t now uses Java-compatible UTF-16 decimal-long parsing, zero fallback and wrapping seconds-to-ms conversion before positive admission. BMP decimal input no longer leaves matching device rows falsely pending for companion cleanup. Exact attribution, earliest-positive time, nullable row versions, immutable original snapshots and reservation guards remain unchanged. Offline regression covers received versus pending companion cleanup/rollback/reopen; fresh live Unicode receipt behavior is unverified. Offline aggregated receipt support (APK 37.71 Cmk.A03/DDF): the first participants child supplies message_id, and each entry supplies its actual jid, independent type (absent defaults to delivery), and required signed BMP-decimal t. Delivery/read/played observations use existing original-target authority and commit as one transaction; malformed input or late saved-state failure commits no partial facts. Inner message_id and per-entry times override root receipt id/type/t in this branch. Unsupported known own/self statuses remain unprojected; the separate key-based participants branch remains unported and cannot fall back to root-id attribution. No original snapshot is backfilled and no resend is authorized. Fresh live aggregate projection remains unverified. HEAD is also served. The parameters listed here are CLI flags; over HTTP the store comes from the serve process. peer_ticket is an unsalted address hash (guessable for phone numbers); treat responses as account data. The local_id path segment is validated before the store opens (400 invalid_input); an ID with no outbox intent answers 404 unknown_local_id.

post.description: CLI-only clock-inspect over the existing encrypted store; no HTTP route. Returns confirmed_source login_success/server_ping/null, resolution elapsed_realtime/saved_offset/inferred_stanza/unavailable and inferred_sample_present. Omits timestamps, offsets, process nonce, raw captures and addresses. Does not adopt historical captures, queue work, contact servers or reset saved clocks. APK 37.71 08B.A04/A07, 0iS.A12/A0y and 1Qt.A02 ground confirmed login and get urn:xmpp:ping inputs. Linux/Android use suspend-aware CLOCK_BOOTTIME with process-scoped elapsed baseline; restart/non-supported hosts use persisted client/server difference. Historical message/receipt sampling remains separate inferred fallback. Full NTP-preferred A00 and token scheduling remain unported. Evidence docs/protocol/token-clock-producers.md. Offline verification; no new live clock validation.

post.summary: Set our profile photo
post.description: Queues `<iq xmlns="w:profile:picture" type="set" to="s.whatsapp.net"><picture type="image">JPEG</picture></iq>` (2.26.37.71 SetProfilePhotoProtocolHelper IXF.A00; own photo has no target; the `to` address is inferred, the builder writes none). The file must be a JPEG (start/end markers) of at most 2 MiB (local bound); the app's crop/resize was not traced, so supply a square JPEG (the app uploads 640x640). A session such as listen transmits it; actions --show reports the reply. No HTTP route is served.

post.summary: Retry once a code request refused as blocked, after exist no longer reports the block
post.description: One explicit live send (requires --allow-live-request). Accepts only a saved code-request refusal with HTTP 200 / reason blocked. Run `lab-signup exist` first: on 2026-11-01 four numbers refused `blocked` in September answered exist with `incorrect`, SMS/voice offered and no wait. The private JSON may correct token, User-Agent, body mode and fields (the legacy-request correction factory); identity and keys are preserved; client_metrics.attempts must equal saved preparations plus one. A durable latch allows one send; a request that provably never left restores the refusal and material. Not a way around a current block or wait.
